articles.title: 7 smart reasons to sell a stock—and my ‘golden rule’ for offloading shares, says hedge fund CEO

paras.en: Nobody is born knowing anything innately about the stock market. And if you feel like you've missed the investing class, you didn't. Usually there isn't one.
paras.zh: 没有人生来就对股票市场有任何了解。如果您觉得自己错过了投资课程，那么您并没有错过。通常是没有的。

paras.en: So responsible people who are trying to do the responsible thing by building a portfolio for themselves and their families often find huge gaps in their knowledge and don't know where to turn.
paras.zh: 因此，那些试图通过为自己和家人建立投资组合来做负责任的事情的负责任的人常常会发现自己的知识存在巨大差距，并且不知道该向何处求助。

paras.en: As the co-founder and CEO of the hedge fund Metropolitan Capital Advisors and a longtime panelist on CNBC's Fast Money, I know that there's no shortage of advice when you're getting started about great investments to buy. It can feel easy and gratifying, especially when your portfolio is doing well. But then things get tougher.
paras.zh: 作为对冲基金 Metropolitan Capital Advisors 的联合创始人兼首席执行官，以及 CNBC Fast Money 的长期小组成员，我知道当您开始购买值得购买的优质投资时，不乏建议。这会让人感到轻松和满足，尤其是当你的投资组合表现良好时。但接下来事情会变得更加困难。

paras.en: One of the hardest things to do as an investor is to figure out when to sell. You buy a stock because you believe it will go up in value. But the decision to sell is rarely so straightforward. Personally, I've made just about every selling mistake. But over time, I've developed a framework for knowing when to sell — and when not to.
paras.zh: 作为投资者最困难的事情之一就是弄清楚何时出售。您购买股票是因为您相信它会升值。但出售的决定很少如此简单。就我个人而言，我几乎犯过所有销售错误。但随着时间的推移，我已经开发了一个框架来了解何时出售以及何时不出售。

paras.en: Selling decisions are often rooted in emotion and cognitive bias rather than logic. One major culprit: anchoring to past performance, a flawed reference point that clouds clear thinking.
paras.zh: 销售决策通常植根于情感和认知偏见，而不是逻辑。罪魁祸首之一：锚定过去的表现，这是一个有缺陷的参考点，模糊了清晰的思维。

paras.en: Behavioral economics, particularly prospect theory, shows that we experience the pain of a loss more intensely than the joy of a gain. This leads investors to cling to losers ("just need to get back to even") and sell winners too early ("lock in the gain").
paras.zh: 行为经济学，特别是前景理论表明，我们经历损失的痛苦比获得的喜悦更强烈。这导致投资者紧紧抓住失败者（“只需要回到平衡”）并过早卖出获胜者（“锁定收益”）。

paras.en: We also place too much emphasis on recent events, a phenomenon known as recency bias. If your last tech stock soared, you're more likely to chase another. If your last trade flopped, you may avoid the market altogether. And when recent trades go well, people tend to trade more — often to their detriment.
paras.zh: 我们还过于强调最近发生的事件，这种现象被称为新近度偏差。如果你的最后一只科技股飙升，你更有可能追逐另一只。如果您的上一次交易失败了，您可能会完全避开市场。当最近的交易顺利时，人们往往会进行更多的交易——这往往会对他们造成损害。

paras.en: Finally, selling triggers a storm of second-guessing and rationalization. Here are my responses to common excuses:
paras.zh: 最后，抛售引发了一场事后猜测和合理化的风暴。以下是我对常见借口的回应：

paras.en: - "What if I'm wrong and it goes up?" What if you're right and it keeps going down?
paras.zh: - “如果我错了并且价格上涨怎么办？”如果你是对的并且股价持续下跌怎么办？

paras.en: - "What will I do with the cash?" You don't always need to put it to work right away, or you can buy a little more of what you already own.
paras.zh: - “我要用这些现金做什么？”您并不总是需要立即将其投入使用，或者您可以购买更多您已经拥有的东西。

paras.en: - "If I double down and it rebounds, I'll make it all back." But if it continues to go down from here, your losses will double.
paras.zh: - “如果我加倍下注并且反弹，我就能全部赚回来。”但如果从这里继续下跌，你的损失将翻倍。

paras.en: - "I don't like having a loss, so I'll sell once it gets back to even." What you originally paid is irrelevant. Yet for many investors, it becomes the most important factor in their decision-making. To assuage their fragile egos, they risk even bigger losses.
paras.zh: - “我不喜欢亏损，所以一旦恢复平衡我就会卖掉。”您最初支付的费用无关紧要。然而对于许多投资者来说，它成为他们决策中最重要的因素。为了安抚他们脆弱的自尊心，他们冒着更大损失的风险。

paras.en: These biases and emotional landmines are why you need a clear, disciplined plan for when to sell, including when:
paras.zh: 这些偏见和情绪地雷是您需要制定清晰、严格的计划来决定何时出售的原因，包括何时：

paras.en: - The original thesis no longer holds. If the fundamental reasons you bought the stock are no longer true — if earnings slow, revenue shrinks, margins deteriorate or the company loses market share — it may be time to move on.
paras.zh: - 原来的论文不再成立。如果你购买股票的根本原因不再成立——如果盈利放缓、收入萎缩、利润率恶化或公司失去市场份额——那么可能是时候离开了。

paras.en: - There's a regulatory risk. Legislative changes can dramatically shift a company's prospects. For example, the outlook for solar-related companies can decline dramatically when tax credits are cut for installations.
paras.zh: - 存在监管风险。立法变化可以极大地改变公司的前景。例如，当安装税收抵免被削减时，太阳能相关公司的前景可能会急剧下降。

paras.en: - Management loses credibility. Frequent earnings misses or misleading guidance suggest deeper problems. One-off surprises happen; recurring surprises reflect poor leadership.
paras.zh: - 管理层失去信誉。频繁的盈利失误或误导性的指导表明存在更深层次的问题。一次性的惊喜会发生；不断出现的意外反映出领导不力。

paras.en: - It becomes too big a slice of your portfolio. A stock that grows from 10% to 25% of your portfolio due to the superb performance of its underlying business, which fuels a soaring stock price, increases your risk from a diversification standpoint. Rebalancing is smart and necessary. The maximum I would have in any one position in my own portfolio is 20% — and that's probably too much!
paras.zh: - 它在你的投资组合中所占的份额太大了。一只股票由于其基础业务的出色表现而从您投资组合的 10% 增长到 25%，从而推动股价飙升，从多元化的角度来看，这会增加您的风险。重新平衡是明智且必要的。我在自己的投资组合中的任何一个头寸的最大比例是 20%——这可能太多了！

paras.en: - The stock becomes overvalued. Sometimes the hype drives prices beyond what fundamentals justify. If valuation detaches from reality, it's okay to take some profits. If it really goes nuts, I will sell enough to take my original investment off the table.
paras.zh: - 股票被高估。有时，炒作会导致价格超出基本面合理范围。如果估值与现实脱节，可以获利了结。如果真的发疯了，我会卖掉足够的钱来收回我最初的投资。

paras.en: - You need the money elsewhere. Selling to fund a home, college tuition or retirement is perfectly valid. Opportunity cost matters.
paras.zh: - 你在其他地方需要钱。出售房屋以资助住房、大学学费或退休是完全有效的。机会成本很重要。

paras.en: - You have tax reasons. For example, tax-loss harvesting may allow you to offset capital gains or deduct up to $3,000 of losses against ordinary income.
paras.zh: - 您有税务原因。例如，税收损失收获可以让您抵消资本利得或从普通收入中扣除最多 3,000 美元的损失。

paras.en: When you've decided to sell for a solid reason — especially the first, second, or third outlined above — don't hesitate. Don't wait for the perfect price. Just sell.
paras.zh: 当您出于充分的原因决定出售时（尤其是上述第一、第二或第三个原因），请不要犹豫。不要等待完美的价格。就卖吧。

paras.en: Just as important as knowing when to sell is knowing when not to sell. Avoid emotionally driven decisions that sabotage long-term gains.
paras.zh: 与知道何时出售同样重要的是知道何时不出售。避免因情绪驱动而做出破坏长期收益的决定。

paras.en: - Don't sell just because it went up. Great companies like Costco, Apple and Microsoft have rewarded patience for decades. Selling too early can mean missing out on compounding returns.
paras.zh: - 不要仅仅因为价格上涨就卖出。 Costco、苹果和微软等伟大公司几十年来的耐心得到了回报。太早出售可能意味着错过复利回报。

paras.en: - Don't sell just because it went down. Market pullbacks are often temporary. If the fundamentals are intact and the decline is market driven, it may be a buying opportunity rather than a reason to exit. Trying to time the market rarely ends well.
paras.zh: - 不要仅仅因为价格下跌就出售。市场回调往往是暂时的。如果基本面完好并且下跌是由市场驱动的，那么这可能是一个买入机会，而不是退出的理由。试图把握市场时机很少有好的结果。

paras.en: - Don't sell because of scary headlines. Economic fears are often priced in before they fully materialize. The market is, forward-looking; headlines usually aren't. Selling during fear often means missing the rebound.
paras.zh: - 不要因为可怕的头条新闻而出售。经济担忧往往在完全实现之前就已被消化。市场是，前瞻性的；头条新闻通常不是。在恐惧中卖出往往意味着错过反弹。

paras.en: Selling well is an advanced investing skill that demands discipline, logic and self-awareness, and there's no place for ego. If you create a sound game plan, you'll be equipped to act confidently, even in the face of uncertainty. I keep a list of reasons to sell handy so I can literally look at it and keep my wits about me.
paras.zh: 做好销售是一项高级投资技能，需要纪律、逻辑和自我意识，并且没有自我的余地。如果您制定了完善的游戏计划，即使面对不确定性，您也将能够自信地采取行动。我在手边保留了一份出售原因清单，这样我就可以逐字逐句地查看它并保持头脑清醒。

paras.en: Karen Finerman is co-founder and CEO of the New York-based hedge fund Metropolitan Capital Advisors and a longtime panelist on CNBC's Fast Money. She is the author of the New York Times bestselling book, "Finerman's Rules: Secrets I'd Only Tell My Daughters About Business and Life" and the host of the podcast How She Does It. Karen is a proud member of the Wharton Board of Advisors, her alma mater, and serves on the board of The Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research.
paras.zh: Karen Finerman 是纽约对冲基金 Metropolitan Capital Advisors 的联合创始人兼首席执行官，也是 CNBC Fast Money 的长期小组成员。她是《纽约时报》畅销书《芬纳曼法则：我只会告诉女儿们关于商业和生活的秘密》的作者，也是播客《她是如何做到的》的主持人。凯伦是她的母校沃顿商学院顾问委员会的荣誉成员，并且是迈克尔·J·福克斯帕金森氏症研究基金会的董事会成员。

articles.title: Nvidia beats on top and bottom lines in first earnings report since Huang's exit: Live updates

paras.en: Nvidia beat on profit and revenue after the bell on Tuesday, in the chipmaker's first earnings report since co-founder Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation last week as CEO.
paras.zh: 周二收盘后，英伟达的利润和收入双双上涨，这是自联合创始人黄仁勋上周突然辞去首席执行官职务以来，该芯片制造商发布的首份盈利报告。

paras.en: Here's how the company did compared to analysts' estimates, according to LSEG:
paras.zh: 根据伦敦证券交易所集团 (LSEG) 的数据，该公司的业绩与分析师的预期相比如下：

paras.en: - EPS: $2.68 adjusted vs. $2.48 expected
paras.zh: - EPS：调整后 2.68 美元，预期 2.48 美元

paras.en: - Revenue: $115.84 billion vs. $109.10 billion expected
paras.zh: - 收入：1,158.4 亿美元，预期为 1,091 亿美元

paras.en: Finance chief Colette Kress is used to addressing Wall Street, but never like this. She's now functioning as interim CEO, meaning her responsibilities go well beyond the key numbers. Employees, investors, analysts and customers are eager to hear her first public remarks since last week's dramatic shake-up.
paras.zh: 财务主管科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）习惯于向华尔街发表讲话，但从来没有像现在这样。她现在担任临时首席执行官，这意味着她的职责远远超出了关键数字。员工、投资者、分析师和客户都渴望听到她自上周剧烈变动以来的首次公开讲话。

paras.en: The earnings call is scheduled to begin at 5 p.m. ET.
paras.zh: 财报电话会议定于下午 5 点开始。等。

paras.en: Nvidia's stock is down 24% this month and on Friday wrapped up its sixth straight weekly drop, the longest losing streak since 2012. The stock has dropped the first two days of this week and is trading at its lowest since July 2025. In addition to the Huang saga, the company is dealing with broader concerns about an AI slowdown and a political shift in Washington, D.C., following this month's midterm elections.
paras.zh: Nvidia 的股价本月下跌了 24%，周五结束了连续第六周下跌，这是自 2012 年以来最长的连续下跌。该股在本周前两天下跌，目前交易价格为 2025 年 7 月以来的最低水平。除了黄蜂事件之外，该公司还面临着对人工智能放缓和本月中期选举后华盛顿特区政治转变的更广泛担忧。

paras.en: The biggest cloud for Nvidia is around its China business after Huang's reported affair with a businesswoman who's allegedly a Chinese spy. The Commerce Department on Monday announced a change that would prevent Nvidia's chips from being rented to Chinese companies entirely, putting revenue at risk.
paras.zh: 在黄与一名据称是中国间谍的女商人有染后，英伟达面临的最大阴云是其中国业务。美国商务部周一宣布了一项改变，将阻止英伟达的芯片完全出租给中国公司，从而使收入面临风险。

articles.title: Widespread outages hit banks, air travel, the NSA and Apple, disrupting seemingly everything

paras.en: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton dismissed suspicions that malicious activity led to a series of outages at major tech firms and government agencies over the last week.
paras.zh: 国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿（Jay Clayton）驳斥了有关恶意活动导致上周主要科技公司和政府机构发生一系列宕机的怀疑。

paras.en: "This is not cyber attack, and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation state," he told CNBC's "Closing Bell" on Tuesday. "We've looked very closely."
paras.zh: “这不是网络攻击，也不是一个民族国家的协调行动，”他周二在 CNBC 的“Closing Bell”节目中表示。 “我们已经非常仔细地观察过。”

paras.en: It's been a tough few days for the technology world after series of widespread disruptions brought different parts of life to a halt.
paras.zh: 在一系列广泛的干扰导致生活的不同部分陷入停顿之后，科技界经历了艰难的几天。

paras.en: On Tuesday, an outage halted internal communications at the National Security Agency and iPhone maker Apple confirmed that different products were either down or having issues.
paras.zh: 周二，国家安全局的内部通信中断，iPhone 制造商苹果公司证实，不同的产品要么出现故障，要么出现问题。

paras.en: The NSA pointed to "scheduled routine maintenance," while Apple cited "an internal update" as the reason behind each issue.
paras.zh: 美国国家安全局指出“定期维护”，而苹果则将“内部更新”作为每个问题背后的原因。

paras.en: It marked four major system problems in four consecutive business days.
paras.zh: 它在连续四个工作日内标记了四个主要系统问题。

paras.en: Microsoft's Outlook issues wreaked havoc on businesses on Thursday, and the Federal Aviation Administration grounded flights on Friday. On Monday, issues at JPMorgan Chase affected customer transactions and an outage at United Airlines briefly delayed departing flights.
paras.zh: 微软的 Outlook 问题周四对企业造成了严重破坏，美国联邦航空管理局周五停飞了航班。周一，摩根大通的问题影响了客户交易，联合航空的停电也导致出发航班短暂延迟。

paras.en: "When Microsoft goes down, the whole world comes to a standstill," said Raj Rajamani, CEO of JetStream Security. "That's a stark reminder of how deeply embedded these services and technologies are in our day-to-day life."
paras.zh: JetStream Security 首席执行官 Raj Rajamani 表示：“当微软倒闭时，整个世界就会陷入停滞。” “这清楚地提醒我们这些服务和技术在我们的日常生活中是多么根深蒂固。”

paras.en: The disruptions have rattled consumers and led to a steady stream of memes on social media, as people look for a silver lining — or sinister plot — in the string of technology problems.
paras.zh: 这些中断让消费者感到不安，并在社交媒体上引发了源源不断的表情包，因为人们在一系列技术问题中寻找一线希望——或者险恶的阴谋。

paras.en: Experts say the real culprit behind this strange series of coincidences is much more benign.
paras.zh: 专家表示，这一系列奇怪的巧合背后的真正罪魁祸首要温和得多。

paras.en: "We're in the weird teenage phase of technology not quite maturing enough to know how to do this without disrupting services and so forth," said Tom Hegel, research head at SentinelOne.
paras.zh: SentinelOne 研究主管 Tom Hegel 表示：“我们正处于技术的奇怪青少年阶段，还不够成熟，不知道如何在不中断服务的情况下做到这一点。”

paras.en: With the help of AI, businesses are patching more software vulnerabilities than ever before and updating archaic systems to prepare for swarms of attacks in the wake of high-profile incidents like Hugging Face.
paras.zh: 在人工智能的帮助下，企业正在修复比以往更多的软件漏洞，并更新陈旧的系统，以应对“拥抱脸”等备受瞩目的事件后的大量攻击。

paras.en: That's leaving IT and security teams strained and scrambling to keep up with heightened demand, said Sam Rubin, SVP of consulting and threat intelligence at Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42.
paras.zh: Palo Alto Networks 的 Unit 42 咨询和威胁情报高级副总裁 Sam Rubin 表示，这使得 IT 和安全团队捉襟见肘，难以满足不断增长的需求。

paras.en: Amid this prolonged period of uncertainty, Rubin said businesses should prioritize updating their most exploitable systems and keeping operations underway when an outage hits.
paras.zh: 鲁宾表示，在这段漫长的不确定时期内，企业应优先更新最可利用的系统，并在停电时保持运营正常进行。

paras.en: "You need to think about how you continue to operate in the face of one of your IT systems going down," he said.
paras.zh: “你需要考虑在 IT 系统出现故障的情况下如何继续运营，”他说。

paras.en: Clayton told CNBC that routine upgrades are commonplace at any organization and called for a nationwide digital infrastructure upgrade.
paras.zh: 克莱顿告诉 CNBC，例行升级在任何组织中都很常见，并呼吁在全国范围内进行数字基础设施升级。

paras.en: Last week, millions of users lost access to email in a fiasco that Microsoft eventually said was the result of an undetected bug that was lurking since July.
paras.zh: 上周，数百万用户无法访问电子邮件，微软最终表示，这是由于自 7 月份以来潜伏的一个未被发现的错误造成的。

paras.en: The FAA, which is still looking into the root cause of the system failure, pointed in part to a router upgrade in southern Arkansas overseen by government contractor L3Harris Technologies that overwhelmed the agency's telecommunications network.
paras.zh: FAA 仍在调查系统故障的根本原因，部分原因是政府承包商 L3Harris Technologies 在阿肯色州南部进行的路由器升级导致该机构的电信网络不堪重负。

paras.en: JPMorgan said longer-than-usual service times on Monday stemmed from a software bug in on-premise hardware systems.
paras.zh: 摩根大通表示，周一的服务时间比平时更长是由于本地硬件系统中的软件错误造成的。

paras.en: Agencies and businesses have ruled out cyber attacks, but the routine patching alibi hasn't satisfied some skeptics, and lawmakers are calling for more transparency.
paras.zh: 各机构和企业已经排除了网络攻击的可能性，但例行修补不在场证据并没有让一些怀疑者满意，立法者呼吁提高透明度。

paras.en: Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., on Tuesday used the recent incidents to make the case for an AI safety bill. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., acknowledged that it's "too premature" to conclude malicious activity but called for a congressional briefing.
paras.zh: 弗吉尼亚州民主党参议员马克·沃纳 (Mark Warner) 周二利用最近发生的事件来论证人工智能安全法案。纽约州众议院少数党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯承认，现在断定恶意活动“为时过早”，但呼吁向国会通报情况。

paras.en: "I think it's time for the administration to come up to the Hill and explain themselves so we can be informed about the steps that need to be taken and we can inform the people of the United States of America," he said during a press conference on Tuesday.
paras.zh: 他在周二的新闻发布会上说：“我认为现在是政府到国会进行解释的时候了，这样我们就可以了解需要采取的步骤，并可以通知美利坚合众国人民。”

articles.title: Betelgeuse and its ‘Betel-buddy’ could light up Earth’s skies

paras.en: One of the night sky’s most storied stars seems to have an even brighter future ahead of it. Betelgeuse—the 10th-brightest star, as seen from Earth, perched at the shoulder of the Orion constellation—has been studied for millennia by generations of stargazers, some of whom saw it shift from yellow to a red hue. Someday this red supergiant star will probably go out in an astrophysical blaze of glory, exploding as a supernova that will light up Earth’s skies. But a new preprint study suggests the iconic star will perform a surprising penultimate flourish before its demise. In a few thousand years’ time, Betelgeuse should swallow its recently revealed companion star and produce a brilliant eruption, shining even brighter than Venus in the heavens above.
paras.zh: 夜空中最著名的星星之一似乎有着更加光明的未来。参宿四是从地球上看第十亮的恒星，位于猎户座的肩部，几代观星者对参宿四进行了数千年的研究，其中一些人看到它从黄色转变为红色。有一天，这颗红色超巨星可能会在天体物理学的荣耀中熄灭，爆炸成超新星，照亮地球的天空。但一项新的预印本研究表明，这位标志性明星在消亡之前将表现出令人惊讶的倒数第二次繁荣。几千年后，参宿四应该会吞噬它最近被发现的伴星，并产生一次辉煌的爆发，其光芒甚至比天空中的金星还要明亮。

paras.en: Betelgeuse has already shown its flare for the dramatic in the past few years. In an event called the star’s “Great Dimming” in 2019, Betelgeuse mysteriously dimmed, seeming like it might explode. Instead astronomers found that it had merely been obscured by dust formed from material it ejected. In recent years researchers also found indications that Betelgeuse harbors a hidden companion star, with some of the most tantalizing evidence emerging just this summer.
paras.zh: 在过去的几年里，参宿四已经展现出了它的戏剧性。在 2019 年一次被称为恒星“大变暗”的事件中，参宿四神秘变暗，看起来可能会爆炸。相反，天文学家发现它只是被其喷射的物质形成的尘埃遮蔽了。近年来，研究人员还发现有迹象表明参宿四拥有一颗隐藏的伴星，其中一些最诱人的证据就在今年夏天出现。

paras.en: As ideas about Betelgeuse and its “Betel-buddy” began to emerge, so did new questions about the duo’s ultimate fate, says Naunet Leonhardes-Barboza, lead author of the paper and a graduate student at the University of California, Santa Cruz. The companion’s presence, it seems, complicates Betelgeuse’s long, now not-so-lonely journey into cosmic night. “Does that mean that the end stages of its life are going to look different now? Are these two stars going to merge?” Leonhardes-Barboza says.
paras.zh: 该论文的主要作者、加州大学圣克鲁斯分校的研究生 Naunet Leonhardes-Barboza 表示，随着有关参宿四及其“槟榔伙伴”的想法开始出现，关于这两者最终命运的新问题也随之出现。同伴的出现，似乎让参宿四漫长而不再那么孤独的宇宙之夜之旅变得更加复杂。 “这是否意味着它生命的最后阶段现在看起来会有所不同？这两颗恒星会合并吗？”莱昂哈德-巴尔博萨说。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: In pursuit of an answer, she and her colleagues modeled how the star system might evolve over time—examining how the companion star could spiral down to its doom, to be torn apart once it is engulfed by Betelgeuse. The team set up simulations for three different possible masses of the companion star—from 0.7 to two times the mass of the Sun—and found that the more massive the companion was, the more energetic and luminous the outburst that was unleashed by its collision would be. All of the modeled masses led to the creation of what astronomers call a luminous red nova. The eruption, which would likely occur within the next 10,000 years, Leonhardes-Barboza says, could be 1.5 to three times brighter than Venus, as it appears from Earth, making Betelgeuse potentially visible even during the daytime. Long after the star’s “Great Dimming” made headlines, it seems that Betelgeuse will bestow a “Great Brightening” on Earthlings, too.
paras.zh: 为了寻找答案，她和她的同事们模拟了恒星系统如何随着时间的推移而演变——研究伴星如何螺旋式下降至毁灭，一旦被参宿四吞没就会被撕裂。研究小组对伴星的三种不同可能质量（太阳质量的 0.7 到两倍）进行了模拟，发现伴星的质量越大，其碰撞所释放的爆发就越有能量和亮度。所有的模型质量都导致了天文学家所说的发光红色新星的产生。 Leonhardes-Barboza 表示，这次喷发可能会在未来 10,000 年内发生，从地球上看，它的亮度可能比金星亮 1.5 到 3 倍，使得参宿四即使在白天也可能可见。在这颗恒星的“大变暗”成为头条新闻很久之后，参宿四似乎也会给地球人带来“大光明”。

paras.en: “For future generations, it’ll be incredible to behold,” says Jared Goldberg, an astrophysicist at the Flatiron Institute’s Center for Computational Astrophysics, who was not part of the study. The experience, Leonhardes-Barboza says, might be akin to how 16th-century stargazers marveled at a supernova—famously noticed by astronomer Tycho Brahe—while it shone brightly in the sky for 16 months. “It would be really noticeable,” Leonhardes-Barboza says. “You’d be like, ‘Whoa, what’s that really bright star there?’” Betegeuse’s brightening, however, would last only a couple days.
paras.zh: “对于子孙后代来说，这将是令人难以置信的，”熨斗研究所计算天体物理中心的天体物理学家贾里德·戈德堡说，他没有参与这项研究。 Leonhardes-Barboza 说，这种体验可能类似于 16 世纪的观星者对超新星的惊叹——天文学家第谷·布拉赫 (Tycho Brahe) 注意到了超新星——它在天空中明亮地闪耀了 16 个月。 “这将非常引人注目，”莱昂哈德斯-巴尔博萨说。 “你会想，‘哇，那颗真正明亮的星星是什么？’”然而，贝特吉斯的明亮只会持续几天。

paras.en: While the episode will certainly be a treat for future generations, the study’s forecast offers insights for today’s astronomers too, Goldberg says. For instance, while Betelgeuse’s proximity to Earth offers us practically a front-row seat to its eventual celestial fireworks, other, farther-off red supergiants might only be detected when they experience similar boosts in brightness. By clearly linking the predicted type of outburst with the anticipated astrophysical merger of Betelgeuse and its Betel-buddy, astronomers can better calibrate their searches for similar events, Goldberg says. “That gives observers a roadmap on how to point their telescopes and search through the data that we’re constantly collecting,” he adds.
paras.zh: 戈德堡说，虽然这一事件肯定会给后代带来欢乐，但该研究的预测也为当今的天文学家提供了见解。例如，虽然参宿四距离地球很近，实际上为我们提供了一个观看其最终天体烟花的前排座位，但其他更远的红超巨星只有在经历类似的亮度增强时才可能被检测到。戈德堡说，通过将预测的爆发类型与参宿四及其同伴的预期天体物理合并明确联系起来，天文学家可以更好地校准他们对类似事件的搜索。 “这为观察者提供了如何瞄准望远镜并搜索我们不断收集的数据的路线图，”他补充道。

paras.en: For Leonhardes-Barboza, the lead-up to Betelgeuse’s great brightening will also be a historic event in its own right. This opportunity to consistently study a premerger system is a rare one, she says: “The fact that we have so much data and knowledge of Betelgeuse’s current state and will be able to follow the system up until the stellar merger—I mean, we don’t have that for anything else.”
paras.zh: 对于莱昂哈德-巴尔博萨来说，参宿四大亮的前奏本身也将是一个历史性事件。她说，这种持续研究合并前系统的机会非常难得：“事实上，我们拥有大量关于参宿四当前状态的数据和知识，并且能够跟踪该系统直到恒星合并——我的意思是，我们没有其他任何东西。”

articles.title: U.S. officially loses measles elimination status in a body blow to public health

paras.en: The U.S. has officially lost its measles elimination status 26 years after it achieved the public health victory.
paras.zh: 美国在取得公共卫生胜利26年后，正式失去了消除麻疹的地位。

paras.en: The announcement by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) on Tuesday formalizes what many experts have been saying is a reality on the ground for months: the U.S. is unable to isolate and contain cases of the highly contagious disease.
paras.zh: 泛美卫生组织（PAHO）周二宣布的消息正式证实了许多专家几个月来一直在说的现实：美国无法隔离和遏制这种高度传染性疾病的病例。

paras.en: So far in 2026 the country has seen more than 5,400 cases of the disease—far outpacing 2025’s 2,289 cases—as well as some 10 deaths. In the years after 2000 and until 2024, the U.S. had typically had fewer than 100 cases per year. But vaccine skepticism and declining childhood vaccine rates have driven the disease’s resurgence—with deadly consequences.
paras.zh: 2026 年迄今为止，该国已出现 5,400 多例这种疾病病例，远远超过 2025 年的 2,289 例，并有约 10 人死亡。从 2000 年到 2024 年，美国每年的病例数通常不到 100 例。但对疫苗的怀疑和儿童疫苗接种率的下降导致了这种疾病的死灰复燃，并带来了致命的后果。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Just 92.4 percent of kindergarteners got the mumps, measles and rubella (MMR) vaccine in the 2025-2026 school year—far below the 95 percent rate needed to maintain herd immunity—with state rates as low as 75 percent. And within states, certain communities have even lower vaccination rates, leading to pockets of spread that have overwhelmed public health protections.
paras.zh: 2025-2026 学年，只有 92.4% 的幼儿园儿童接种了腮腺炎、麻疹和风疹 (MMR) 疫苗，远低于维持群体免疫力所需的 95%，而州接种率低至 75%。在各州内部，某些社区的疫苗接种率甚至更低，导致小范围的传播超出了公共卫生保护措施。

paras.en: “Losing measles elimination status has broader implications than losing a public health designation,” said PAHO director Jarbas Barbosa at a press briefing on Tuesday. “It means the virus has circulated for a prolonged period of time, putting families and communities at risk of preventable illness.”
paras.zh: 泛美卫生组织主任贾巴斯·巴博萨在周二的新闻发布会上表示：“失去麻疹消除地位比失去公共卫生称号具有更广泛的影响。” “这意味着病毒已经传播了很长一段时间，使家庭和社区面临可预防疾病的风险。”

paras.en: The resurgence of measles is “a sobering reminder of what happens when vaccination rates decline and decades of public health progress are reversed,” said American Medical Association president Willie Underwood III in a statement.
paras.zh: 美国医学会主席威利·安德伍德三世在一份声明中表示，麻疹的死灰复燃“清醒地提醒人们，当疫苗接种率下降和几十年的公共卫生进展逆转时会发生什么”。

paras.en: “The resurgence of measles across the country has caused preventable hospitalizations and deaths and reflects the consequences of growing gaps in community protection,” he said. “We must treat the current measles outbreaks as an urgent call to rebuild trust in science-based recommendations and restore strong, fully-funded public health infrastructure to protect families and communities and prevent the return of diseases once eliminated.”
paras.zh: 他说：“麻疹在全国范围内卷土重来，造成了可预防的住院和死亡，反映出社区保护差距日益扩大的后果。” “我们必须将当前的麻疹疫情视为紧急呼吁，以重建对基于科学的建议的信任，并恢复强大的、资金充足的公共卫生基础设施，以保护家庭和社区，并防止疾病一旦消除后卷土重来。”

paras.en: In the wake of the decision, some public health experts singled out U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., for particular criticism. Kennedy is a longtime vaccine skeptic and has repeatedly linked the MMR vaccine to autism despite the lack of any good evidence for such a connection.
paras.zh: 该决定做出后，一些公共卫生专家特别批评了美国卫生与公众服务部部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪。肯尼迪长期以来一直对疫苗持怀疑态度，并多次将 MMR 疫苗与自闭症联系起来，尽管缺乏任何有力的证据证明这种联系。

paras.en: “RFK Jr. has spent over a decade trying to destroy disease prevention, the last two as HHS secretary, and his public health malpractice is coming home to roost,” said Gregg Gonsalves, a Yale School of Public Health researcher and a member of the health advocacy group Defend Public Health’s coordinating committee, in a statement. “Congress can no longer sit back and twiddle its thumbs.”
paras.zh: 耶鲁大学公共卫生学院研究员、健康倡导组织捍卫公共卫生协调委员会成员格雷格·贡萨尔维斯在一份声明中表示：“小罗伯特·肯尼迪花了十多年的时间试图破坏疾病预防，最后两年担任卫生与公众服务部部长，他的公共卫生不当行为正在受到应有的惩罚。” “国会不能再袖手旁观。”

paras.en: In a statement to Scientific American, a Department of Health and Human Services spokesperson defended Kennedy and said that the department has provided states with $100 million in funding to combat measles outbreaks under his leadership.
paras.zh: 在给《科学美国人》的一份声明中，卫生与公众服务部发言人为肯尼迪辩护，并表示该部门已向各州提供了 1 亿美元的资金，用于在他的领导下抗击麻疹疫情。

paras.en: Critics, however, say HHS—and particularly, the department’s Centers for Disease Control and Prevention—has failed to implement a unified, coordinated, nationwide vaccination campaign or to combat vaccine misinformation.
paras.zh: 然而，批评者表示，美国卫生与公众服务部，尤其是该部门的疾病控制与预防中心，未能实施统一、协调的全国性疫苗接种运动，也未能打击疫苗错误信息。

paras.en: Quantifying the role of misinformation in the outbreaks is difficult, said PAHO’s Barbosa, but the organization is working with member countries to provide more information to health care workers on the efficacy and safety of vaccines.
paras.zh: 泛美卫生组织的巴博萨表示，量化错误信息在疫情中的作用很困难，但该组织正在与成员国合作，向医护人员提供更多有关疫苗功效和安全性的信息。

paras.en: “It’s very well known that the main source that families take into account to make their decision to vaccinate is the information provided by nurses and physicians,” Barbosa said. “[Health ministries] need to be prepared to respond to misinformation, providing clear, transparent information to the families and communities, so they can make the best decision.”
paras.zh: 巴博萨说：“众所周知，家庭在决定接种疫苗时考虑的主要来源是护士和医生提供的信息。” “[卫生部]需要做好应对错误信息的准备，向家庭和社区提供清晰、透明的信息，以便他们能够做出最佳决定。”

paras.en: Daniel Salas, PAHO’s executive manager for immunizations, said at the same press event that the U.S. has already begun intensifying vaccination efforts, particularly in areas with low coverage that have ongoing active transmission of measles. But the country needs to submit a corrective action plan that offers more detail on how it intends to fight the outbreaks in order to begin the process toward regaining its elimination status, he said.
paras.zh: 泛美卫生组织负责免疫接种的执行经理丹尼尔·萨拉斯在同一次新闻发布会上表示，美国已经开始加强疫苗接种工作，特别是在麻疹持续活跃传播的覆盖率低的地区。但他说，该国需要提交一份纠正行动计划，提供更多关于打算如何抗击疫情的细节，以便开始恢复消除状态的进程。

paras.en: “According to this framework, we are expecting the U.S. to present this corrective plan of action in the coming weeks,” Salas said. That could involve strategies such as increased surveillance to detect new cases early, rapid response to limit outbreaks and efforts to vaccinate at-risk populations.
paras.zh: 萨拉斯说：“根据这一框架，我们预计美国将在未来几周内提出这一纠正行动计划。”这可能涉及加强监测以及早发现新病例、快速反应以限制疫情爆发以及努力为高危人群接种疫苗等策略。

paras.en: “This necessitates the deployment of teams and adequate lab laboratory support, and these things require funding,” said PAHO’s assistant director Rhonda Sealey-Thomas.
paras.zh: 泛美卫生组织助理主任朗达·西利-托马斯表示：“这需要部署团队和足够的实验室支持，而这些都需要资金。”

paras.en: The decision to revoke the U.S.’s elimination status comes a year after PAHO made the same call for Canada, as that country dealt with an outbreak that led to more than 5,000 cases and two deaths. In response, the Canadian government launched a vaccination campaign in communities with historically low immunization rates, and in October it declared the outbreak to be over. Canada must go a year without measles cases spreading before it can regain its elimination status, however. (It recently reached the 60-day mark.) PAHO had also previously revoked elimination status from Venezuela and Brazil in 2018 and 2019, respectively, but their status was later restored.
paras.zh: 在决定撤销美国的消除地位一年前，泛美卫生组织对加拿大发出了同样的呼吁，因为该国正在应对导致 5,000 多例病例和两人死亡的疫情爆发。对此，加拿大政府在免疫率历史较低的社区发起了疫苗接种运动，并于10月宣布疫情结束。然而，加拿大必须在一年内没有麻疹病例蔓延，才能恢复消除麻疹的状态。 （最近已达到 60 天大关。）泛美卫生组织此前还分别于 2018 年和 2019 年撤销了委内瑞拉和巴西的消除地位，但后来恢复了它们的地位。

paras.en: The U.S. is far from alone in this setback: the U.K., Mexico, Bolivia, Spain, Austria, Armenia, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan also lost their measles elimination status this year.
paras.zh: 美国并不是唯一遭遇这一挫折的国家：英国、墨西哥、玻利维亚、西班牙、奥地利、亚美尼亚、阿塞拜疆和乌兹别克斯坦今年也失去了消除麻疹的地位。

paras.en: Editor’s Note (11/17/26): This is a breaking news story and may be updated.
paras.zh: 编者注（11/17/26）：这是一个突发新闻报道，可能会更新。

articles.title: Infinitesimals are essential to calculus. But are they even real?

paras.en: Last week, I recounted how Isaac Newton and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz laid the foundations for calculus—and how they relied on the curious concept of infinitesimal quantities to do so. But infinitesimals, understood to be immeasurably small—almost but not quite zero in value—have been a challenging concept for mathematicians to accept.
paras.zh: 上周，我讲述了艾萨克·牛顿和戈特弗里德·威廉·莱布尼茨如何奠定微积分的基础，以及他们如何依靠无穷小量这个奇怪的概念来做到这一点。但无穷小，被理解为不可估量的小——价值几乎但不完全为零——对于数学家来说一直是一个难以接受的概念。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Archimedes considered this concept centuries before either Newton or Leibniz. He defined infinitesimals as follows: |dt| < 1/1, |dt| < 1 / (1 + 1), |dt| < 1 / (1 + 1 + 1),... And even having defined them, he doubted these quantities could actually exist.
paras.zh: 阿基米德比牛顿或莱布尼茨早几个世纪就考虑了这个概念。他将无穷小定义如下： |dt| < 1/1，|dt| < 1 / (1 + 1), |dt| < 1 / (1 + 1 + 1),... 即使定义了它们，他也怀疑这些量是否真的存在。

paras.en: Some mathematicians, such as Guillaume de l’Hôpital, were convinced of the existence of infinitesimals. Leibniz and Newton, however, expressed themselves more cautiously, despite relying on the concept in their work. Leibniz did not claim that the unusual quantities actually existed but that correct conclusions could be drawn with their help. Newton went further. Although his calculations in his book Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica were based on infinitesimals, he replaced them with ordinary calculations or simply omitted them before publication.
paras.zh: 一些数学家，例如纪尧姆·德·霍皮塔尔，坚信无穷小的存在。然而，莱布尼茨和牛顿尽管在他们的工作中依赖于这个概念，但表达得更加谨慎。莱布尼茨并没有声称这些异常量确实存在，但可以在它们的帮助下得出正确的结论。牛顿走得更远。尽管他在《自然哲学数学原理》一书中的计算是基于无穷小，但他在出版前用普通计算代替了它们，或者干脆省略了它们。

paras.en: Meanwhile, in 1734, philosopher George Berkeley critiqued infinitesimals, noting that even the tiniest values played a crucial role in mathematics. From Berkeley’s perspective, calculating velocity at a specific moment—a crucial step in Newton’s work—would never give us an exact velocity but instead an approximation. He wrote, “They are neither finite quantities, nor quantities infinitely small, nor yet nothing. May we not call them the ghosts of departed quantities?”
paras.zh: 与此同时，1734 年，哲学家乔治·伯克利 (George Berkeley) 批评了无穷小，指出即使是最小的值在数学中也发挥着至关重要的作用。从伯克利的角度来看，计算特定时刻的速度（牛顿工作中的关键一步）永远不会给我们一个精确的速度，而是一个近似值。他写道：“它们既不是有限的量，也不是无限小的量，也不是什么也不是。我们可以不称它们为已逝量的幽灵吗？”

paras.en: In the 19th century German mathematician Karl Weierstrass found a way around infinitesimals altogether. To define quantities such as velocity at fixed times, as Newton did, or to calculate the area under a curve, as Leibniz demonstrated, Weierstrass used limits. This approach circumvented the problem but led to stilted definitions, such as: v is the desired velocity if, for every ε > 0, the magnitude of Δs ⁄ Δt = – v is less than ε for all values of |Δt | < δ, where δ > 0. Such epsilon-delta definitions are typically taught today in undergraduate courses. They work well but are not particularly elegant.
paras.zh: 19 世纪，德国数学家卡尔·威尔斯特拉斯 (Karl Weierstrass) 找到了一种完全解决无穷小问题的方法。为了像牛顿那样定义固定时间的速度等量，或者像莱布尼茨所证明的那样计算曲线下的面积，韦尔斯特拉斯使用了极限。这种方法规避了这个问题，但导致了生硬的定义，例如：如果对于每个 ε > 0，对于所有 |Δt | 值，Δs ⁄ Δt = – v 的大小都小于 ε，则 v 是所需速度。 < δ，其中 δ > 0。如今，此类 epsilon-delta 定义通常在本科生课程中教授。它们工作得很好，但不是特别优雅。

paras.en: Yet infinitesimals continued to be used. In fact, numerous advances have been made in physics and applied mathematics as a result.
paras.zh: 然而无穷小仍然被继续使用。事实上，物理学和应用数学因此取得了许多进步。

paras.en: In the 1960s mathematician Abraham Robinson succeeded in developing a mathematical theory of infinitesimals. He built upon the abstract insights of mathematician Kurt Gödel, who had found a way to use the tools of mathematics to reflect on the discipline itself.
paras.zh: 20 世纪 60 年代，数学家亚伯拉罕·罗宾逊 (Abraham Robinson) 成功发展了无穷小数学理论。他建立在数学家库尔特·哥德尔的抽象见解之上，哥德尔找到了一种使用数学工具来反思学科本身的方法。

paras.en: Gödel's basic idea follows: a specific area of the discipline, such as standard calculus, can be considered a “universe,” M; we use a language, L, to make statements about such universes, including formulas and formal statements, each of which can be true or false. For example: 1 + 1 > 1 is true. All false statements can be negated so that they, too, become true statements—at least theoretically. (In reality, we don’t know all the true or false statements.)
paras.zh: 哥德尔的基本思想如下：学科的一个特定领域，例如标准微积分，可以被认为是一个“宇宙”，M；我们使用语言 L 来对这样的宇宙做出陈述，包括公式和形式陈述，其中每一个都可以是真或假。例如：1 + 1 > 1 为真。所有错误的陈述都可以被否定，以便它们也成为正确的陈述——至少在理论上是这样。 （事实上​​，我们并不知道所有的真假陈述。）

paras.en: If you collect every true statement of L, including the negated false ones, you create a single set, K. This set is the complete theory of M, a universe in which everything in Kholds true. But Gödel’s work makes it clear that K can have other models, such as M*. These models may be built from entirely different objects than M but obey the same relationships such that every statement in K remains true.
paras.zh: 如果你收集 L 的每个真陈述，包括否定的假陈述，你就创建了一个集合 K。这个集合是 M 的完整理论，在这个宇宙中 K 中的一切都成立。但哥德尔的工作清楚地表明，K 可以有其他模型，例如 M*。这些模型可能是由与 M 完全不同的对象构建的，但遵循相同的关系，使得 K 中的每个陈述都保持正确。

paras.en: Let’s use an example to think that through further. Suppose M consists of all the fish within a lake. You can make all sorts of true statements about these aquatic animals, such as that one of the fish can swim faster than another. You can then imagine M* as the entire lake, including not just the fish but the water as well. Every statement about M could still apply to M*, even though the latter contains more than M.
paras.zh: 让我们用一个例子来进一步思考。假设 M 由湖中的所有鱼组成。您可以对这些水生动物做出各种真实的陈述，例如其中一条鱼比另一条鱼游得更快。然后，您可以将 M* 想象为整个湖，不仅包括鱼，还包括水。关于 M 的每个陈述仍然适用于 M*，即使后者包含的内容比 M 多。

paras.en: In the same way, standard calculus with real numbers, M, can be extended to a larger universe, M*, which contains new kinds of numbers. Robinson developed this line of thinking using two core statements of logic:
paras.zh: 同样，实数 M 的标准微积分可以扩展到更大的宇宙 M*，其中包含新类型的数字。罗宾逊使用两个核心逻辑陈述发展了这一思路：

paras.en: - Completeness: a set of logical statements is consistent—meaning free of contradiction—if and only if a universe exists in which they are all true. (This idea also comes from Gödel.)
paras.zh: - 完整性：一组逻辑陈述是一致的——意味着没有矛盾——当且仅当存在一个它们都为真的宇宙时。 （这个想法也来自哥德尔。）

paras.en: - Compactness: if every finite subset of a collection of statements is consistent, the whole collection is consistent, however large it may be. If you can satisfy any finite set of statements at once, there must exist a universe where every single statement holds simultaneously.
paras.zh: - 紧凑性：如果语句集合的每个有限子集都是一致的，则整个集合是一致的，无论它有多大。如果您可以同时满足任何有限的陈述集，则必须存在一个宇宙，其中每个陈述同时成立。

paras.en: That second tenet is essential to creating infinitesimals. If we go back to Archimedes, he essentially described an infinitely small quantity as: |dt| < 1/1, |dt| < 1 / (1 + 1), |dt| < 1 / (1 + 1 + 1).... In our ordinary universe of real numbers, no number |dt| satisfies every one of these at once—which is why Archimedes doubted the existence of infinitesimals. But any finite handful of these statements is comparatively easy to satisfy. By compactness, that makes the entire infinite collection consistent. That means there must be some universe where all of these statements are true simultaneously. In that universe, |dt| is a genuine infinitesimal: it is smaller than every ordinary positivenumber yet is not zero. (The same line of thinking, run in reverse, leads to a universe in which infinitely large numbers also exist.)
paras.zh: 第二个原则对于创造无穷小至关重要。如果我们回到阿基米德，他基本上将无限小的量描述为：|dt| < 1/1，|dt| < 1 / (1 + 1), |dt| < 1 / (1 + 1 + 1).... 在我们普通的实数宇宙中，没有数字 |dt|同时满足所有这些——这就是阿基米德怀疑无穷小是否存在的原因。但这些陈述中任何有限的几个都相对容易满足。通过紧凑性，这使得整个无限集合保持一致。这意味着必须存在某个宇宙，所有这些陈述同时成立。在那个宇宙中，|dt|是一个真正的无穷小：它比每个普通正数都小，但不为零。 （同样的思路，反向运行，会导致宇宙中也存在无限大的数字。）

paras.en: So is everyone convinced? As I’ve written before, there are mathematicians who reject the concept of infinity. But most see infinities and infinitesimals as valid mathematical structures, even if they don’t always map easily onto our day-to-day reality. Meanwhile Robinson’s nonstandard calculus, in which infinitesimals exist, has not yet gained widespread acceptance. Although the theory is certainly interesting, calculations in this area are often extremely complex. Standard calculus methods are usually more suitable for proving its existence.
paras.zh: 那么大家都信服了吗？正如我之前所写，有些数学家拒绝无穷大的概念。但大多数人将无穷大和无穷小视为有效的数学结构，即使它们并不总是容易映射到我们的日常现实中。与此同时，罗宾逊的非标准微积分（其中存在无穷小）尚未获得广泛接受。尽管该理论确实很有趣，但该领域的计算通常极其复杂。标准微积分方法通常更适合证明它的存在。
