articles.title: How Paper-Based Friction Materials Power Modern Machinery

paras.en: How Paper-Based Friction Materials Power Modern Machinery

Have you ever wondered what enables everything from roaring construction machinery to agricultural machinery plowing the fields to industrial equipment shuttling through factories—the precise starting, smooth operation, and reliable braking they achieve?

The answer lies in a seemingly insignificant yet crucial core component: friction material. It acts as the "safety guard" and "power link" of machinery, ensuring every brake is safe and effective, and every power transmission is smooth and flawless.

Among the vast family of friction materials, wet friction materials are becoming the new favorite in modern machinery due to their exceptional reliability, safety, and exceptionally long lifespan. Among wet materials, paper-based friction materials stand out as a leading force thanks to their excellent overall performance, cost-effectiveness, and broad application prospects.
Today, let's delve deeper into the fascinating world of this "unsung hero"—paper-based friction materials.
What is Paper-Based Friction Material? — A Sponge-Like Power Core
Imagine a "sponge" with countless tiny pores—that's the most intuitive image of paper-based friction material.

It is a material with a reticular porous structure composed of three core components: reinforcing fibers, functional fillers, and a binder resin. This unique structure gives it extraordinary capabilities:
- Oil Storage Capacity: The porous structure acts like a miniature "oil depot," capable of storing large quantities of lubricant.

- Dynamic Lubrication: When the friction plate and mating plate engage and are subjected to pressure, the lubricant within the material is instantly squeezed onto the friction surface, forming a tough lubricant film, enabling smooth, gentle "wet" friction.
- Self-Recovery: When the friction plates separate, the material rebounds like memory foam, "absorbing" the lubricant back into the pores, ready for the next operation.

It is this dynamic cycle of "oil storage-oil squeezing-oil return" that allows paper-based friction materials to perform well in an oil bath environment, achieving a perfect combination of high durability and stable friction performance.
Exploring Core Performance: How Do Three Key Factors Affect It?

The performance of paper-based friction materials is not static. Like a top athlete, its performance is influenced by the "field," "equipment," and "condition." Let's examine how these three key factors shape its performance.
Factor 1: The "Stage Effect" of Lubricants

Paper-based friction materials are highly sensitive to lubricants, and different lubricants create distinct "stages" for their performance. Even the same friction material can exhibit significantly different friction characteristics (especially the kinetic friction coefficient) when exposed to different lubricants.
Figure 1: Kinetic friction coefficient curve for a paper-based friction material in gear oil
Figure 2: Dynamic friction coefficient curve of the same material in hydraulic oil

Interpretation: The above chart clearly shows that the same material behaves very differently in gear oil and hydraulic fluid. Furthermore, various additives added to lubricating oils (such as dispersants and anti-wear agents) can interact complexly with the material surface, further affecting its friction properties. Therefore, choosing the right oil for paper-based friction materials is the first step in achieving optimal performance.
Density is a trump card for paper-based friction materials. It is directly related to the material's porosity, leading to a delicate balancing act in terms of performance.

High density (low porosity) means a denser material, resulting in better strength and thermal conductivity, lower wear rate, and longer life. However, the downside is reduced oil storage capacity, which can lead to a lower coefficient of friction and compromise power transmission.

Low density (high porosity) means the material is more porous, resulting in greater oil storage capacity and a higher coefficient of friction, which can provide greater braking force or transmit torque. However, the downside is reduced mechanical strength and wear resistance, shortening service life.
Figure 3: Comparison of the dynamic coefficient of friction for materials of varying densities (Type 2 to Type 6, increasing density)
Figure 4: Comparison of wear rates of materials with different densities

Interpretation: Figures 3 and 4 vividly illustrate this balancing act. There's no such thing as absolute good or bad, only suitability. When selecting a paper-based friction material, the optimal trade-off between friction coefficient and durability must be determined based on specific application requirements (e.g., high torque versus long life).
Factor 3: Extreme Challenges of Operating Conditions

In addition to oil type and density, actual operating conditions, such as surface pressure, sliding speed, and oil temperature, pose extreme challenges to paper-based friction materials. These factors directly affect the temperature of the friction interface, the thickness and stability of the oil film, and thus dynamically alter the coefficient of friction.

Therefore, please remember: the coefficient of friction of a particular paper-based friction material is not a fixed value, but rather a performance range determined through extensive and repeated testing under specific operating conditions.
Broad Applications: Injecting a Powerful "Heart" into Machinery

Thanks to its excellent overall performance and customizability, Carlisle Brake & Friction's paper-based friction materials have been successfully applied to the core components of various heavy-duty machinery, becoming their powerful and reliable "heart."
We understand that different machines and applications require significantly different friction materials. For example:
- Service brakes for construction machinery (such as excavators and loaders) require materials that provide a stable, powerful braking force under high loads to ensure safety.
- Powershift transmissions for agricultural machinery (such as tractors) require materials that provide smooth engagement and excellent heat resistance to handle frequent shifting.
- Clutches for industrial machinery require materials that respond quickly and have a long lifespan to ensure continuous and efficient operation of production lines.

To this end, Carlisle Brake & Friction has developed a series of special paper-based friction materials for different application scenarios, providing each customer with the most suitable and reliable solution.
Continuous Innovation, Driving the Future
Technological advancement is endless. To meet increasingly demanding application requirements and broaden market prospects, Carlisle Brake & Friction remains at the forefront of innovation.

We are not only continuously optimizing the formulation and processing of paper-based friction materials to push their performance limits, but are also actively exploring next-generation wet friction materials with even higher performance. These R&D efforts have made significant progress, aiming to provide global customers with more diverse and advanced options, driving the infinite possibilities of future machinery.

articles.title: Pirelli prepares for cold-weather tyre management challenge at Las Vegas Grand Prix
articles.author: Andrew

paras.en: Pirelli prepares for cold-weather tyre management challenge at Las Vegas Grand Prix

Formula 1’s exclusive tyre supplier Pirelli faces one of the most technically demanding rounds of the 2026 season this weekend as the championship heads to Nevada for the fourth edition of the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Held at night on the 6.201km Las Vegas Strip Circuit, the event presents unique environmental hurdles for tyre performance. With air temperatures forecast between 10 and 15°C due to wide desert day-night swings, keeping rubber within its optimal operating window will be paramount. The circuit’s three long full-throttle straights reduce energy transfer into the tyres, making warm-up particularly critical during Friday qualifying, where teams may rely on consecutive preparation laps to preserve surface temperatures.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Track evolution will further complicate Pirelli’s data modelling. Because the street circuit reopens to public traffic daily, dust and sand continually reset grip levels, alongside minor resurfacing repairs carried out ahead of Turn 13 and on the approach to Turn 14. While overall lateral loads remain moderate outside the high-speed middle sector, the combination of cool asphalt and low initial grip leaves tyres susceptible to mechanical degradation and graining. Heavy braking zones at the end of the straights also heighten the risk of front lock-ups and flat-spotting.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: On paper, Pirelli anticipates a one-stop strategy to be the quickest route through Saturday night’s race, with all three nominated dry compounds, including the versatile C5, capable of playing a strategic role. However, traditional undercut tactics are expected to be less effective, as fresh tyres rapidly lose temperature along the extended run from the pit exit before reaching higher-load corners. Should wet weather return as it did during last year’s qualifying session, Pirelli notes that the deeper tread of the Full Wet tyre is particularly suited to generating and retaining heat on the cool street surface compared to the Intermediate.

paras.en: In last year’s race, all three podium finishers executed one-stop strategies, starting on the yellow-marked Medium compound before completing the distance on the C3 Hard.

Away from the technical operations in the pit lane, Pirelli is also leveraging the high-profile event for its commercial lifestyle division. The Italian manufacturer has unveiled a special edition Las Vegas Grand Prix Podium Cap, created by Denis Dekovic for Pirelli Design. Inspired by the constellations of the Nevada desert night sky, the release is already available to consumers via Pirelli’s online store.

articles.title: Opus IVS, asTech Introduce CarDAQ NXT Diagnostic Device
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: Opus IVS and asTech have introduced CarDAQ NXT, a compact collision diagnostic device designed to help technicians navigate vehicle scanning and service requests. Modeled on the DriveSafe wizard, the device walks technicians through vehicle identification and repair information before directing them to the appropriate next step.

CarDAQ NXT provides access to OE scans, supported IVS scans and additional service requests through a step-by-step process. The system captures key details, including VIN, repair order, insurance information and whether the scan is being performed before or after a repair. A dedicated asTech Connect option displays a QR code technicians can scan to access asTech Connect on a separate compatible device.

“Collision repair technicians need tools that make it easier to navigate diagnostic processes and access the services required for each repair,” said Brian Herron, CEO of asTech, Opus IVS and BlueDriver. “CarDAQ NXT brings these steps together in a straightforward process, helping shops establish a consistent approach to diagnostics across their teams.”

Built on the CarDAQ Pro/ScanSafe hardware platform, CarDAQ NXT features a compact 5-inch screen for shops that prefer a smaller device. The home screen also provides access to device, network and account settings. CarDAQ NXT requires shop-provided internet connectivity to access connected services.
For more information on Opus IVS, visit opusivs.com.
For more information on asTech, visit asTech.com.

paras.en: Daniele said the company’s commercial business has evolved significantly as it continues investing in the professional repair market. With commercial sales approaching $6 billion and programs in approximately 95% of its stores, AutoZone is strengthening its product quality, availability and delivery capabilities to better serve repair shops. Daniele emphasized the importance of OE-quality or better products, including its Duralast portfolio, alongside expanded assortments through its hub and mega hub strategy. Investments in technology, inventory optimization and a dedicated professional sales force are helping AutoZone get the right parts to shops faster while building stronger customer relationships.

The company also celebrated its 1,000th store in Mexico, expanded distribution capabilities there and broke ground on another facility. articles.title: The Cost of Knowing It All: Why Smart Body Shop Owners Never Stop Learning
articles.author: Erkan OZ

paras.en: There was a time when experience was the most valuable tool a body shop owner had. Years spent repairing vehicles, managing technicians and solving problems taught you what worked and what didn’t. You learned by doing, watching others and occasionally making a mistake you promised yourself you’d never repeat.
That experience still matters. But today, experience alone isn’t enough.

The collision repair industry is changing faster than ever. Vehicle technology is advancing, repair procedures are more complicated and running a profitable shop takes more knowledge than it did even a few years ago.
For shop owners, continuing to learn isn’t just about keeping up with technology. It’s about building a stronger business, developing better employees and making smarter decisions.
The shops that succeed won’t necessarily be the ones that know everything today. They’ll be the ones willing to keep learning tomorrow.
The Collision Industry Isn’t Slowing Down

Think about how much collision repair has changed over the past 20 years. Today’s vehicles have ADAS, cameras, sensors, radar, high-strength materials and increasingly complicated electronics. Electric and hybrid vehicles bring additional safety and repair considerations.

A repair that once seemed straightforward may now require specialized equipment, manufacturer procedures and additional training. Getting it wrong can affect more than customer satisfaction. It can put vehicle safety, your reputation and your business at risk.

Owners don’t need to become experts in every repair procedure. But they do need to understand enough to ask the right questions, make smart equipment investments and ensure their technicians have access to current repair information.
Training can’t be something you think about only when there’s extra time or money. It needs to be part of how your shop operates.

And there’s one phrase that should probably disappear from every repair facility: “We’ve always done it this way.” Experience is valuable, but so is being willing to change your approach when there’s a better way.
Technical training is only part of the picture. The owner sitting in the office has just as much to learn as the technician working on a vehicle.
Running a collision repair business requires financial knowledge, production management, estimating, customer service, marketing and leadership skills. And all those areas affect one another.
Consider a shop that’s busy from morning until closing. Cars are coming in, technicians are working and the schedule is full. Yet somehow, the owner isn’t making the money expected. Sound familiar?
Maybe work in progress is piling up. Parts delays are slowing production. Supplements are taking too long, or labor hours aren’t producing the expected gross profit.
Being busy doesn’t automatically mean you’re profitable.

An owner who understands financial statements, key performance indicators, cash flow and production management can identify what’s really happening. Instead of working longer hours or pushing employees harder, that owner can make changes based on facts.

Leadership is another area where owners often need help. Many shop owners learned how to repair vehicles long before they learned how to manage people. They may be terrific technicians but struggle with delegating, developing managers or holding employees accountable.
The good news is that leadership can be learned.
Better communication, stronger management skills and a clearer understanding of how to motivate employees can make an enormous difference.
You don’t have to become an expert overnight. Just keep getting better at running your business.

Ask collision repair owners about their biggest challenges and finding good employees will almost certainly make the list. Qualified technicians are difficult to find, and keeping them can be just as challenging.

One way to address both problems is to create a workplace where people have opportunities to learn and advance. Employees want to know they have a future. When you invest in their development, you’re showing them that they’re important to the business.

And training doesn’t always mean sending someone to an expensive class. It can be mentoring a younger technician, reviewing a new repair procedure as a team, cross-training employees or giving someone an opportunity to learn a different part of the operation.
An experienced technician might share valuable repair knowledge with a newer employee. That younger employee might introduce a more efficient digital tool or diagnostic technique.
Of course, training costs money. It also takes employees away from production. But consider what happens when you don’t train.
Mistakes, rework, wasted materials, safety problems and frustrated employees can cost far more.

Not every training investment will produce an immediate financial return. Sometimes the payoff is a more confident employee, a safer repair or someone who’s better prepared to take on additional responsibility.
It’s easy to get so caught up in daily operations that you stop paying attention to what’s happening outside your business.

The phone rings. A customer needs an update. A part hasn’t arrived. An insurance approval is holding up a repair. Before you know it, another day has disappeared. That’s why it’s important to occasionally get away from the day-to-day problems and see what other shop owners are doing.
Industry conferences, training programs, peer groups and association meetings can introduce you to ideas you might never discover on your own.

Sometimes a conversation with another owner is worth more than hours spent trying to solve a problem yourself. How does another shop manage production? What are they doing to recruit employees? How did they develop a successful manager? What have they learned about expanding their business?
You don’t have to copy someone else’s operation. But you might discover an idea that works for yours.
Industry publications, webinars and educational resources can also help you stay informed without constantly leaving the shop.
The important thing is to do something with what you learn. Reading an article or attending a seminar is a good start. Putting one useful idea into practice is even better.
Most customers won’t ask how many training classes you’ve attended or what certifications your employees hold. But they’ll notice the results.

They notice when someone answers the phone promptly, explains a repair clearly and keeps them informed. They notice when promised timelines are realistic and when employees seem to know what they’re doing.
And they certainly notice when things go wrong.
Training in communication and customer service helps employees handle difficult conversations and explain complicated repairs in ways customers can understand.
Better estimating and production management help the shop provide accurate updates and avoid unnecessary surprises.
Technical training and quality control help ensure repairs are performed properly.

Remember, most customers aren’t happy about needing collision repairs in the first place. They’re dealing with an accident, insurance questions and the inconvenience of being without their vehicle. They want reassurance that they’ve chosen the right shop.
A knowledgeable, professional team goes a long way toward earning that trust. And when customers trust your business, they’re more likely to recommend it to others and leave positive reviews.
One of the biggest reasons owners don’t invest more time in learning is simple: They’re busy.
There’s always something more urgent to handle.
You plan to attend a webinar, review financial reports or read about a new repair procedure. Then the day gets away from you.
Waiting until things slow down probably isn’t going to work. For most collision repair shops, that day never comes.
It doesn’t have to take hours every week. Start small.

Spend a little time reviewing your numbers. Read an industry article. Talk with your team about a repair challenge. Watch a training video or ask another owner how they handled a problem you’re facing. Then set a larger goal for each quarter.
Maybe you want to better understand your financial statements, improve production efficiency or develop someone who could eventually become your general manager.
Whatever you choose, connect the learning to something practical.
If you attend a seminar, come back with one idea to try. If an employee completes training, have that person share what was learned with the team.
And pay attention to the results. Did the change improve efficiency? Reduce mistakes? Make someone’s job easier? Improve customer communication?
If it worked, keep doing it. If it didn’t, figure out why.
Learning should lead to improvement, not just another certificate hanging on the wall.
And don’t be afraid to admit when you don’t know something.
Asking for help or advice isn’t a weakness. It’s often the smartest decision an owner can make.
Build a Business That Doesn’t Depend on You
There’s another important reason to keep learning and developing your people.

Eventually, you may want to expand, step back from daily operations or sell your business. But what happens if you’re the only person who understands the financials, makes every decision and solves every problem?

You’ve built a business that depends entirely on you. That’s not a particularly comfortable position to be in, especially if you’d like to enjoy the rewards of everything you’ve worked so hard to create. A learning culture helps change that.
When employees develop new skills, managers learn to make decisions and systems are put in place, the business becomes less dependent on one individual.
You’re building a team that can handle challenges without waiting for you to provide every answer.
That makes the shop easier to manage today and potentially more valuable tomorrow.
It also gives you something many owners struggle to find: freedom.
The goal should be to own a business, not simply create a job that requires you to be there every minute.
Collision repair isn’t an easy business. There are employees to manage, customers to satisfy, vehicles to repair and bills to pay.
And just when you think you’ve figured everything out, something changes. That’s not going away.
But the more you and your employees learn, the better prepared you’ll be to handle whatever comes next.
You don’t need to know everything. You just need to stay curious and be willing to improve.
- What do I need to learn to become a better owner?
- What skills would help my employees succeed?
- What could we do differently that would make this a stronger business?
The vehicles will keep changing. Technology will keep advancing. Customers will continue to expect more.
You can’t control all those changes, but you can control how prepared your shop is to handle them.

Sometimes the best investment you can make isn’t another piece of equipment or a bigger facility. It’s investing in yourself and your people. Because a shop that never stops learning is a shop that gives itself every opportunity to keep growing.

articles.title: Building a roadmap for your technicians covered in IDEAS Collide
articles.author: Lurah Lowery

paras.en: As a 2026 Society of Collision Repair Specialists IDEAS Collide Showcase presenter, Maria Quintero, Body Builders Automotive owner, shared the importance of mapping out technician careers so collision repair shops can guide them toward their goals with proper training and incentives to learn, grow, and advance.

“Everybody here wants to know where we are, where we started, and where we’re going,” she said. “I think it’s just human nature, and our technicians are no different… The reality is we want to see growth, and our technicians want to know: how do I get there?”
The annual showcase was held Nov. 4 in Las Vegas as part of this year’s SEMA Show.

According to statistics Quintero shared from a September 2026 Robert Half survey, 55% of Gen Z professionals (ages 14–29) said they plan to look for a new job by year-end. Half said the reason was limited advancement. Fifty-three percent said they believe the way to make more money is to change employers.
Quintero also cited Resume.org survey findings from December 2025, which found 45% of Millennials (ages 30–45) were considering a job change.

“What does that translation look like for us? If a young technician sees a path to make more money and they don’t see it at your shop because we haven’t developed that roadmap, they’re going to assume that that path is down the street or not even in this industry,” Quintero said. “A roadmap answers that question before they can even go looking. We have to own the work, and we have to share the return.”
Before building the “technician roadmap,” Quintero said shops need to understand the operation they want their technicians to succeed in, and the numbers behind it.

In Quintero’s example, a shop’s annual sales goal is $4 million, with labor at 48% of that. That’s $1,920,000 to work with and a $768,000 gross profit. Now, fit the tech’s numbers in. The tech wants to make $85,000; that’s 11% of the shop’s total labor cost budget. For the tech to be paid $85,000, the shop needs to bring in $212,500 in labor sales. Nine techs earning that amount would meet the shop’s labor goal.
Here’s Quintero’s breakdown of building out the roadmap:
- Set an operation: What’s the skill that the technician is going to be tested on?
- Criteria: What’s the testing period? What does it take to pass?
- Pay rate: Start rate, raise per skill, and rate after.
- Trainer bonus: Pay your senior technicians to grow the next technician.
Remember, efficiencies with the shop and the techs build together, she said.

“On the profitability side, for the shop, we know revenue beating expenses is going to make us money; we all know that,” Quintero said. “For the technician, though, what is their personal ROI? What is their return on that investment? They invest their time, energy, and skill, and they should get paid. Their growth and their career: what does that look like? When the shop is profitable, it can churn the next rate increase.”

Maybe you start a new tech out in disassembly. From there, they can advance and move through each stage, meeting benchmarks to go on to the next position. And with each skill set achieved comes a pay raise, Quintero said.

“You’re giving them a roadmap of saying, ‘Your next pay increase isn’t dependent on how I feel about you. It isn’t dependent on if I like you this week or not. It’s dependent on how you showed up at work. What is the skill set you learned? I believe that if you bring the right attitude, you’re going to get the right output, but you got to have that in place… The raise is tied to the skill. It’s not tied to who asks the loudest, learns faster, or earns faster.”
Quintero shared four rules shops can follow to give techs unbiased raises based on their career progression:
- Test solo: No help from another technician.
- Checkpoint: A-tech or foreman signs off at each stage.
- Pass twice: One good repair isn’t a skill; two is.
- Set rates: Clear and non-negotiable, with the same rules for everyone.
She added that, along the way, training is built in based on each shop’s preferences for what should be learned and when.

“My challenge I ask of all of you is to go back and build yourselves a roadmap by listing the skills for every position in the shop, add a test and a raise to every skill, and then tie it back to your numbers,” Quintero said.
Featured image: Maria Quintero speaks during the 2026 SCRS IDEAS Collide Showcase. (Lurah Lowery/Repairer Driven News)

articles.title: State Farm agrees to $45 million settlement with Oklahoma for claims handling
articles.author: Teresa Moss

paras.en: State Farm Fire and Casualty Company has agreed to more than $45 million in settlement following an investigation by the Oklahoma Insurance Department (OID) into the company’s handling of homeowners’ claims for wind and hail damage to roofs, according to an OID press release.
The settlement followed OID releasing a market conduct examination Friday, that found State Farm improperly denied or failed to pay for roof damage and necessary repairs on claims.

As a result, State Farm agreed to a settlement that includes a minimum of $35 million dedicated to making affected consumers whole, $10 million for Oklahoma’s Strengthen Oklahoma Homes grant program and an additional $2.86 million in fines and examination expenses payable to the department.

Eligible Oklahoma homeowners who had a claim for wind and hail damage closed without payment between Jan. 1, 2001 and Dec. 31, 2025 will have another opportunity to have their claims independently reviewed, the release states.
The release defines “closed without payment” as including claims that received partial payment or were determined to be under the deductible amount.

“Our responsibility is to stand up for Oklahoma consumers, and that means holding insurance companies accountable when they fail to meet their obligations to policyholders,” said Insurance Commissioner Glen Mulready in the release. “We weren’t willing to simply take State Farm’s word for how these claims were handled. We took action that no other state has done in a traditional examination, putting independent engineers in the field to inspect roofs and help determine whether claims were handled appropriately.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: State Farm will establish a claim reopening process at its own expense, the release states. An independent third-party claims administrator, mutually selected by OID and State Farm will review each eligible claim. This will include evaluating the original claim file and any additional documentation or evidence submitted by the policyholder.
If an administrator determines that a claim qualifies for payment, State Farm will pay the claim in accordance with the insured’s individual policy, the release states.
State Farm and OID will agree upon an additional amount of funds, if more funds are needed to pay all claims, the release adds.

Eligible homeowners will receive written notices from State Farm that have been approved by OID. It will explain the review process and how to opt in.The Department also plans to help educate consumers throughout the process.

“I cannot stress enough how important it is for eligible homeowners to take advantage of this opportunity and opt in,” Mulready said. “If your roof claim was closed without payment during this period, don’t assume the decision was the final word. This process gives eligible Oklahomans another chance to have their claims independently evaluated. We want consumers to know this opportunity is real, understand how to participate, and have confidence that their claims will receive an independent review.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The $10 million donated to the department’s Strengthen Oklahoma Homes grant programs will help Oklahoma consumers strengthen their homes against severe weather by installing fortified roofs designed to better withstand Oklahoma’s weather conditions. Homeowners who participate are seeing an average homeowners’ insurance premium savings of $700.
Additional information about eligibility, timelines, and the claims review process will be released as details are finalized.
If you have questions about other insurance issues, please contact the Oklahoma Insurance Department at 800-522-0071 or visit their website at www.oid.ok.gov.

articles.title: Law firm analysis finds airbag defects the deadliest vehicle defect
articles.author: Teresa Moss

paras.en: A Florida law firm’s analysis on recall and consumer complaints regarding vehicle defects found faulty airbags pose the greatest risk to consumers with about 500 deaths in a decade.

“Most drivers don’t think about a defect until it shows up on the road, and by then they’re dealing with it at speed,” Steven Frankl, attorney with Frankl Kominsky Injury Lawyers, says in an email. “The parts that cause the most harm are often the ones you never notice working, right up until the moment you need them.”

The November report, completed by Frankl Kominsky Injury Lawers examined 39 vehicle defect categories across the U.S. from airbags and brakes to steering and electrical systems. It counted the safety recalls tied to each category between 2015 and 2025. The number of consumer complaints, crashes, injuries, and deaths were pulled from the federal documents, the law firm says in an email.

“These figures were combined into a single score out of 100, with deaths weighted most heavily, followed by injuries and crashes, showing which defects are tied to the most serious outcomes for drivers,” the email says.

Airbags received a score of 100 with 97,700 complaints and 494 deaths. Electrical systems received the next highest score of 42, with 126,700 complaints and 209 deaths. Vehicle speed control received a score of 31, with 29,300 complaints and 267 deaths.

Airbag defects range from defective inflators and sensors to trouble with deployment, including airbags that fail to go off during crashes, the email states. Airbags had 114 million recalls between 2015 and 2025.
Electrical systems include wiring, batteries, electrical connections, and components, according to the email. There were 1,535 safety recalls between 2015 and 2025, the email adds.
“A fault in one of them can stop the system it belongs to from working,” the email states.
Speed control defects included cruise control, acceleration, and throttle responses.
“A defect here can leave a car speeding up or slowing down on its own, without any input from the driver,” the email states.
It adds that complaints about speed control defects included 2,336 injuries.
Service brakes were the third most dangerous defect in the report, receiving a score of 28, with 58,800 complaints and 93 deaths.

“This category covers general brake problems, from poor brake performance to faults in how the brake system operates, and hydraulic, air, and electric brake parts fall into categories of their own,” the email states. “For a driver, that means a car that does not slow down or stop the way it should when the pedal is pressed.”
There were 6,410 crash reports for brake defects, the email adds and 3,529 injuries were reported.
Engine trouble ranked as the fifth most dangerous with a risk score of 27. There were 132,900 complaints filed and 125 deaths connected to the defects.
“The category takes in engines that stall, run unreliably, or do not perform the way they should, and engine cooling problems are counted as a separate defect,” the email states.
Frankl adds that a recall letter deserves the same attention as a warning light on the dashboard.

“If the car brakes, speeds up, or steers in a way that feels wrong, write down what happened, report it, and get it looked at,” Frankl adds. “Every complaint adds to the record, and that record helps get problems fixed for the next driver.”
NHTSA announced earlier this month that it will invest $1.5 million to help states improve vehicle recall rates to keep roads safe.

“A vehicle with an open recall creates an avoidable hazard on our roads,” said NHTSA Administrator Jonathan Morrison in a news release. “By giving states the resources to flag open recalls when drivers register or renew their vehicles, we can keep dangerous cars off our roads and American families safe.”

NHTSA learned during the Takata airbag recalls that convincing consumers to remedy a recall is complicated, he said. Researchers found some consumers were confused about what the recall meant or simply didn’t remember receiving the notices.

Lee White, NHTSA’s deputy administrator, said during the Society of Collision Repair Specialists’ (SCRS) OEM Summit held during the 2026 SEMA Show last week, that collision repairers are the final checkpoint for roadway safety.
One way repairers can be a checkpoint for vehicle defects on safety systems is by performing vehicle inspections.

Mike Anderson, Collision Advice co-owner, said during a Collision Industry Conference meeting earlier this year that every OEM manufacturer has procedures in their electric service manuals (ESM) that state inspections need to be done when a vehicle is in a collision. He said this could include inspections of seatbelts, steering columns, and airbags.

Anderson said that the industry is minimizing the importance of safety inspections. He said there has been recent focus on ADAS calibrations, but safety inspections are just as, if not more, important.

“At the end of the day, the OEM says it needs to be done,” Anderson said. “At the end of the day, the insurance company doesn’t want to pay for it. The shop is stuck in the middle. Nobody wants to indemnify the shop. It is just wrong; it is wrong on every level.”
If a shop is found liable for not following OEM procedures, it could be sued and lose everything, Anderson added.

articles.title: Collision or Custom: Body Shop Career Opportunities
articles.author: Bud Center

paras.en: In the automotive world, few disciplines bridge the gap between traditional and artistry like custom painting. While collision repair painters work with precision to return vehicles to their original form, custom painters approach each surface as a canvas — layering colors, textures and effects to create something extraordinary.

From the complex environment of matching OEM finishes to the unpredictable dance of candy coats, metallics and chameleon pearls, the journey requires more than technical know-how — it demands vision, patience and an unrelenting eye for detail.

This article will explore the profound differences between collision repair painting and custom refinishing, highlighting the unique challenges, techniques and skills that define the art of custom automotive paint.

While there is substantial skill and knowledge crossover between OEM refinishing and custom work, custom colors are inherently more demanding to apply. This stems from their heightened sensitivity to spray technique, more complex layering systems and increased visual complexity, all of which require a different level of control and precision from the painter.

The challenges in the auto painting world are numerous, and while collision repair and custom painting share some core technical hurdles, the nature, tolerance and consequence of those challenges differ.

While both disciplines demand skill, planning and product knowledge, collision repair painting requires consistency, speed and compliance with OEM and product maker requirements, while custom painting prioritizes artistry, depth and absolute surface control. The margin for error is narrow in both — but the visual consequences of an error are often magnified in custom work.

Experience is a critical factor for any painter and one of the most critical factors when it comes to custom painting. In fact, I think most would agree that time spent practicing, failing, refining techniques and mastering materials is what separates average results from award-winning finishes.

Proper prep work is critical in both collision repair and custom painting, as both disciplines demand precision, cleanliness and attention to substrate quality. However, in custom applications, prep takes on an even greater level of importance, due to the sensitivity of finishes like candies, metallics, pearls, flakes, tri-stage effects, airbrushed graphics and pinstriping. These systems tend to amplify even the smallest surface irregularities — such as sanding halos, micro-scratches or inconsistent featheredges — which can distort flake orientation, compromise color clarity or telegraph visibly through transparent layers.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: While these concerns also apply in collision repair, the tolerance for imperfection in custom work is far lower, meaning that minor flaws in prep can result in major flaws in the final finish.

The automotive refinish world encompasses a broad spectrum of finish types, and in many cases, the finish is more than just color — it’s about depth, dimension and visual presence. Whether the objective is to create subtle sophistication or bold, attention-grabbing effects, custom refinish work expands the palette of techniques and material systems far beyond standard formulas. This includes finishes such as metallics, pearls, multi-stage systems, candies, flakes and color-shifting (chameleon) effects. Each of these systems introduces specific requirements related to spray technique, substrate preparation, environmental control and post-application finishing — all of which demand a disciplined, detail-oriented approach from the refinisher.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Automotive painting sits at the crossroads of craftsmanship, chemistry and creativity, demanding a unique combination of technical precision, product knowledge and — in many cases — artistic sensibility. While collision refinishing focuses on accuracy, efficiency and restoration of OEM appearance, custom painting pushes into a different realm — where each finish is built to stand out, not blend in. From the controlled sparkle of metallics and pearls to the depth-driven complexity of candy colors and the layered illusion of custom graphics and airbrush work, it’s a discipline where experience, preparation and consistency aren’t just important — they’re the foundation of success. In the collision booth, the goal is to restore what was lost; in the custom booth, it’s to create something entirely new. Both demand excellence — just in different forms.

articles.title: Why Tire Pressure is Important When Gas Prices Rise
articles.author: Christian Hinton

paras.en: With gas prices high, customers may be looking for ways to stretch a tank of fuel. Tire pressure is one factor that can affect fuel economy. Underinflated tires create more rolling resistance, forcing the engine to work harder to keep the vehicle moving.

According to the U.S. Department of Energy, gas mileage can decrease by about 0.2% for every 1 PSI drop in the average pressure of all four tires. Keeping tires properly inflated can improve fuel economy by up to 3%.
For automotive repair shops, proper tire inflation provides an opportunity to educate customers about fuel economy and tire maintenance.
Maintaining proper tire pressure can help customers save fuel, reduce unnecessary tire wear and extend tire life.

articles.title: Superchargers: How They Work and What Techs Need to Know
articles.author: Doug Kaufman

paras.en: Superchargers have long been associated with high-horsepower engines, drag racing and performance vehicles. But for future automotive technicians, understanding superchargers involves more than knowing how they make power.
paras.zh: 增压器长期以来一直与大马力发动机、直线加速赛和高性能车辆联系在一起。但对于未来的汽车技术人员来说，了解增压器不仅仅是知道它们如何产生动力。

paras.en: These forced-induction systems increase the amount of air entering an engine, allowing it to burn more fuel and produce additional horsepower and torque. While superchargers can deliver strong throttle response, they also create challenges involving efficiency, heat and mechanical load.
paras.zh: 这些增压系统增加了进入发动机的空气量，使发动机能够燃烧更多的燃油，从而产生更多的马力和扭矩。虽然增压器可以提供强劲的油门响应，但它们也会带来与效率、热量和机械负荷相关的挑战。

paras.en: Learning how different supercharger designs operate can help students understand engine performance and prepare for real-world diagnostic work.
paras.zh: 学习不同增压器设计的运作方式，可以帮助学生了解发动机性能，并为实际的诊断工作做好准备。

paras.en: A supercharger compresses incoming air before it enters the engine’s cylinders. The increased air density allows more oxygen into the combustion chambers, supporting greater fuel delivery and increased power output.
Most conventional superchargers use a belt driven by the engine’s crankshaft to operate the compressor.

This mechanical connection is one of the biggest differences between a supercharger and a turbocharger. A turbocharger uses exhaust gas energy to drive its compressor, while a traditional supercharger draws power directly from the engine.
That difference affects throttle response, efficiency and the way each system delivers boost.

Tech Tip: Boost pressure is the amount of intake pressure above atmospheric pressure. However, higher boost does not automatically mean greater power. Intake air temperature, airflow, engine efficiency and calibration also affect performance.
Roots-Style Superchargers: Strong Low-RPM Response
A Roots-style supercharger, often called a blower, typically mounts above the intake manifold and uses two rotating lobed rotors to move air into the engine.
As the rotors turn, they carry air from the inlet to the outlet. The pressure increases primarily when the air enters the pressurized intake system.
Roots-style superchargers are known for delivering strong low-speed response. However, the design can generate significant heat, especially at higher pressure ratios.
Modern Roots-style systems may use intercooling to reduce intake air temperatures and improve performance.

What Students Should Know: Roots-style blowers are positive-displacement devices. That means they move a relatively consistent volume of air during each revolution, making them effective at delivering low-rpm torque.
Twin-Screw Superchargers: Improving Compression Efficiency
Twin-screw superchargers may look similar to Roots-style units, but they operate differently.
Instead of primarily moving air into a pressurized outlet, twin-screw superchargers use specially shaped rotors to compress air internally as it travels through the housing.
This design can improve compression efficiency and reduce discharge temperatures compared with traditional Roots-style designs under comparable operating conditions.
Twin-screw systems are frequently used in high-performance applications where strong power delivery across a broad engine-speed range is desirable.

What Students Should Know: Although Roots-style and twin-screw superchargers both use rotating lobed components, their methods of compressing air differ. Understanding that distinction helps explain differences in temperature, efficiency and power delivery.
Centrifugal Superchargers: Building Boost With Engine Speed
A centrifugal supercharger works differently from the positive-displacement designs.
It uses a high-speed impeller to accelerate incoming air. A diffuser then converts much of that air velocity into pressure before the air enters the engine.
The compressor design is similar to the compressor side of a turbocharger. However, a centrifugal supercharger is usually driven mechanically rather than by exhaust gases.
Because compressor speed is tied to engine speed, centrifugal systems generally produce less boost at lower rpm and progressively more boost as engine speed increases.
These characteristics make centrifugal superchargers useful in applications that emphasize higher-rpm performance.
What Students Should Know: Not all superchargers deliver the same low-rpm boost. Students should understand how compressor design affects the engine’s power curve.
Electric Superchargers: Another Approach to Boost
Electric compressors represent another approach to forced induction.

Rather than relying on a belt driven by the crankshaft, these systems use an electric motor to drive the compressor. Some applications use a 48-volt electrical architecture to supply the power needed for rapid compressor operation.
Electric compressors can help improve boost response at lower engine speeds, particularly when used with exhaust-driven turbochargers.
Unlike a traditional belt-driven supercharger, the system draws energy from the vehicle’s electrical system. That energy still has to be generated and managed.

What Students Should Know: Electrically driven compressors introduce electrical diagnosis into forced-induction service. Technicians may need to understand power supply, control circuits, motor operation and manufacturer-specific safety procedures.
The Advantages and Disadvantages of Superchargers
Superchargers can improve engine performance, but their benefits come with trade-offs.
- Strong throttle response, particularly with positive-displacement designs.
- Predictable boost characteristics based on compressor design.
- No exhaust-driven turbine or associated turbocharger wastegate system in a conventional belt-driven installation.
- Belt-driven systems consume some engine power, creating parasitic loss.
- Compressing air increases intake air temperature.
- Increased cylinder pressure and heat place additional demands on engine components.
- Drive belts, pulleys, bearings and cooling components introduce additional service considerations.
- Fuel consumption may increase, depending on engine calibration and driving conditions.
For technicians, understanding these trade-offs is important when diagnosing performance complaints or evaluating modifications.
What Should Technicians Inspect on a Supercharged Engine?
A vehicle equipped with a supercharger may arrive with complaints such as reduced power, unusual noise or inconsistent boost.
Before replacing components, technicians should understand how the system operates and follow the manufacturer’s diagnostic procedures.
On belt-driven applications, examine the supercharger belt, pulleys and tensioner for wear, damage or misalignment.
A slipping belt can reduce compressor speed and affect boost delivery.
Inspect intake ducting, connections and related components for loose fittings, cracks or leaks.
On applications with pressurized intake plumbing, leaks can reduce boost and cause performance problems.
Compressing air creates heat. When equipped with an intercooler or charge-air cooling system, verify that its components operate correctly.
Excessive intake temperatures can reduce performance and contribute to engine knock.
Depending on the vehicle, technicians may be able to monitor manifold absolute pressure (MAP), intake air temperature (IAT), fuel trim and other engine operating data.
Compare measurements with manufacturer specifications and operating conditions rather than assuming a particular boost value is correct for every vehicle.
After completing a repair, verify that the system operates properly and that the original complaint has been corrected.
Follow approved service procedures for any testing that requires the engine to operate under load.
Classroom Connection: Comparing Supercharger Designs
Instructors can use supercharger technology to connect engine theory with real-world performance applications.
Have students compare Roots-style, twin-screw and centrifugal superchargers. Ask them to identify how each system moves air, develops boost and affects engine performance.
- Why does a belt-driven supercharger create parasitic loss?
- How does a twin-screw supercharger differ from a Roots-style blower?
- Why does a centrifugal supercharger generally develop more boost as engine speed increases?
- How can elevated intake air temperatures affect performance?
- What diagnostic steps would you take if a supercharged engine produced less boost than expected?

For a hands-on exercise, students can inspect a training engine or examine manufacturer service information to identify the supercharger drive system, intake routing, pressure sensors and charge-air cooling components.
This exercise helps reinforce engine performance theory while building inspection and diagnostic skills relevant to future technicians.
Superchargers offer a practical example of how mechanical design, airflow and engine management work together to increase performance.
Roots-style, twin-screw, centrifugal and electric systems each have distinct operating characteristics, advantages and service considerations.
For automotive students, the goal is not simply to recognize the different designs. It is to understand why they behave differently and how those differences affect diagnosis and service.
The next time you encounter a supercharged engine, consider this: How does its compressor design affect power delivery, efficiency and the problems a technician might need to diagnose?

articles.title: Autel Awards Five Automotive Education Scholarships
articles.author: Alex Crissey

paras.en: Autel announced five recipients of its second annual Awarding Excellence Scholarships. The scholarships are part of Autel Cares, the company’s philanthropic initiative supporting automotive education and community causes.
paras.zh: Autel 宣布了第二届年度卓越奖学金的五位获奖者。这些奖学金是Autel Cares的一部分，这是该公司支持汽车教育和社区事业的慈善计划。

paras.en: The 2026 program awards five $5,000 scholarships, totaling $25,000. The awards support students pursuing education and training in automotive repair and service.
paras.zh: 2026年计划将颁发五笔5,000美元的奖学金，总额为25,000美元。该奖学金旨在为接受汽车维修和服务方面教育和培训的学生提供支持。

paras.en: Recipients can use the scholarships for tuition, tools, books, supplies and other education-related expenses. The students are preparing for careers in the automotive repair industry.
paras.zh: 获奖者可以将奖学金用于学费、工具、书籍、用品和其他与教育相关的开支。这些学生正在为从事汽车维修行业的职业生涯做好准备。

paras.en: This year, Autel expanded eligibility beyond recent high school graduates. Adult learners returning to school or transitioning from another career also qualified.
paras.zh: 今年，Autel 将资格范围扩大到了近期高中毕业生以外的人群。重返校园的成人学员或从其他职业转行的学员也符合资格。

paras.en: The 2026 recipients represent students at different stages of life and training. Their interests include automotive technology, collision repair, manufacturer-level service and automotive cybersecurity.
paras.zh: 2026年获奖者代表了处于不同人生阶段和培训阶段的学生。他们的兴趣包括汽车技术、碰撞维修、制造商级服务和汽车网络安全。

paras.en: “Last year, selecting our first scholarship recipients was difficult. This year was even more challenging because we received so many outstanding applications from students with compelling stories, clear goals, and a genuine commitment to automotive education,” said Chloe Hung, CEO of Autel U.S.
paras.zh: “去年，选出首批奖学金获得者并不容易。今年难度更大，因为我们收到了许多优秀学生的申请，他们有着引人入胜的故事、明确的目标，以及对汽车教育的真诚承诺。”Autel美国首席执行官Chloe Hung表示。

paras.en: “The five recipients selected this year reflect the many different paths people take into the automotive repair industry, from students beginning their training to adults continuing or returning to school. Autel is proud to support their education and invest in the skilled professionals who will help shape the future of automotive repair.”
paras.zh: “今年选出的五位获奖者反映了人们进入汽车维修行业的多种不同途径，从刚开始接受培训的学生到继续学业或重返校园的成年人。Autel很荣幸能够为他们的学业提供支持，并投资于将帮助塑造汽车维修未来的技术专业人才。”

paras.en: The 2026 Autel Awarding Excellence Scholarship recipients are:
paras.zh: 2026年Autel卓越奖学金获得者名单如下：

paras.en: - Shawn Clark, of Deer Lodge, Montana, attends Highlands College of Montana Tech. Clark is beginning a new chapter in automotive education at age 50. He is pursuing an associate degree in automotive technology. His application reflects this year’s expanded eligibility for adult learners returning to school. Clark plans to build a new career in automotive repair.
paras.zh: - 来自蒙大拿州迪尔洛奇的Shawn Clark就读于蒙大拿理工大学高地学院。Clark在50岁时开启了汽车教育的新篇章。他正在攻读汽车技术副学士学位。他的申请反映了今年重返校园的成年学员资格的扩大。Clark计划在汽车维修领域开创新的职业生涯。

paras.en: - Jacob Heinrichs, of Austin, Texas, attends Universal Technical Institute of Texas Inc. Heinrichs already works in the field and has three years of experience as an automotive technician. His selection reflects Autel’s support for working technicians seeking additional training. Heinrichs aims to advance his skills and career opportunities.
paras.zh: - 来自德克萨斯州奥斯汀的 Jacob Heinrichs 就读于德克萨斯州通用技术学院。Heinrichs 已在该领域工作，并拥有三年汽车技师经验。他的入选反映了Autel对希望接受更多培训的在职技术人员的支持。Heinrichs 的目标是提升自己的技能和职业机会。

paras.en: - Marisa Rueger, of Harleysville, Pennsylvania, attends Automotive Training Center-Warminster. Rueger is pursuing collision repair and holds a 4.0 GPA. In her application, she described collision repair as her art. She also emphasized her desire to continue learning, growing and succeeding in the field.
paras.zh: - Marisa Rueger来自宾夕法尼亚州哈利斯维尔，就读于沃明斯特汽车培训中心。Rueger正在攻读碰撞维修专业，GPA为4.0。在申请书中，她将碰撞维修描述为自己的艺术。她还强调了自己希望继续学习、成长并在这个领域取得成功的愿望。

paras.en: - Logan Mercier, of Claremont, California, attends Universal Technical Institute of California Inc. Mercier aims to complete school with a 4.0 GPA. He also plans to build advanced diagnostic skills and work toward becoming a master technician. His application focuses on academic achievement, professional growth and building a career in automotive repair.
paras.zh: - 来自加州克莱蒙特的Logan Mercier就读于加州通用技术学院。Mercier的目标是以4.0的GPA成绩毕业。他还计划培养高水平的诊断技能，并努力成为一名高级技师。他的申请重点在于学业成绩、专业成长以及在汽车维修领域发展职业生涯。

paras.en: - Kristof Adam, of Stillwater, Minnesota, attends Century College. Adam is pursuing a career in automotive cybersecurity. He has a strong interest in hands-on vehicle work and advanced automotive technology. His application highlights the growing importance of technical education as vehicles become more connected, complex and software-driven.
paras.zh: - Kristof Adam来自明尼苏达州斯蒂尔沃特，就读于Century College。Adam正在从事汽车网络安全方面的职业。他对车辆的实际操作和先进的汽车技术有着浓厚的兴趣。他的申请突显了随着车辆变得更加互联、更加复杂和更加由软件驱动，技术教育的重要性日益凸显。

paras.en: Applicants submitted either a 500- to 600-word essay or a two- to three-minute video. They described the path that led them to pursue automotive repair education.
paras.zh: 申请人提交了500至600字的论文或2至3分钟的视频。他们描述了自己走上汽车维修教育之路的历程。

paras.en: Applicants also explained how the scholarship would support their training. They discussed their goals, obstacles and planned careers in the automotive repair industry.
paras.zh: 申请人还阐述了奖学金将如何为他们的培训提供支持。他们讨论了各自的目标、障碍以及在汽车维修行业的职业规划。

articles.title: Momentum USA Adds 12 Brake Part Numbers
articles.author: Alex Crissey

paras.en: Momentum USA added 12 new part numbers to its brake friction and rotor catalog. This update expands coverage to over 5.3 million Vehicles in Operation (VIO) across North America.
paras.zh: Momentum USA在其刹车摩擦片和刹车盘目录中新增了12个零件编号。此次更新将覆盖范围扩展至北美地区超过530万辆在用车辆（VIO）。

paras.en: The new products include rotors for luxury and performance vehicles, and expanded offerings for Hyundai, Kia and Honda vehicles.
paras.zh: 新产品包括用于豪华车和高性能车的刹车盘，以及为现代、起亚和本田汽车提供的更多产品。

paras.en: A more detailed list of import applications is as follows:
paras.zh: 更详细的进口申请清单如下：

paras.en: - Hyundai, Kia & Honda: Expanded coverage across models including the Hyundai Palisade, Santa Fe, and Santa Cruz; Kia Sorento and Carnival (PTC2381); as well as the Honda HR-V and Honda Clarity (PRC2116 / CE2116).
paras.zh: - 现代、起亚和本田：扩大了车型覆盖范围，包括现代帕利塞德、圣达菲和圣克鲁斯；起亚索兰托和嘉华（PTC2381）；以及本田HR-V和本田Clarity（PRC2116/CE2116）。

paras.en: - Mercedes-Benz, Land Rover & Volvo: Added seven new Coated and R90 Euro Rotor SKUs to serve luxury sedans, sports coupes, and performance SUVs—including Mercedes-Benz S-Class, SLK, and C-Class models, Land Rover Defender and Range Rover Sport models (537200), and the Volvo XC60 (521480).
paras.zh: - 奔驰、路虎和沃尔沃：新增了七款涂层和R90 Euro刹车盘SKU，适用于豪华轿车、跑车和高性能SUV，包括奔驰S级、SLK和C级车型、路虎卫士和揽胜运动版车型（537200）以及沃尔沃XC60（521480）。

articles.title: How Regenerative Braking Changes Repair and Inspection
articles.author: Joe Keene

paras.en: Regenerative braking allows electric vehicles to recover energy during deceleration. Instead of converting all vehicle momentum into heat at the brake rotors, the electric motor acts as a generator. This slows the vehicle while returning some energy to the battery.
paras.zh: 再生制动使电动汽车能够在减速过程中回收能量。电机充当发电机，而不是将车辆的所有动能都转化为制动盘上的热能。这会使车辆减速，同时将部分能量返回到电池中。

paras.en: The process can significantly reduce the use of conventional friction brakes. However, reduced brake usage can also create maintenance challenges involving corrosion and component operation.
paras.zh: 该过程可以显著减少传统摩擦制动器的使用。然而，减少制动器的使用也可能带来与腐蚀和部件运行相关的维护难题。

paras.en: On conventional internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles, brake pads regularly contact the rotors during braking. This friction helps remove light surface corrosion from the rotor faces.
paras.zh: 在传统的内燃机（ICE）车辆上，制动片在制动过程中会定期与制动盘接触。这种摩擦有助于去除制动盘表面轻微的锈蚀。

paras.en: EVs with aggressive regenerative braking may use their friction brakes less frequently. Exposure to moisture, road salt and humidity can then allow corrosion to develop on the rotor surfaces.
paras.zh: 配备强力再生制动的电动汽车可能较少使用其摩擦制动器。因此，如果刹车盘表面接触到水分、道路盐分和潮湿环境，就可能发生腐蚀。

paras.en: EV Regenerative Braking and Rotor Corrosion
paras.zh: 电动汽车再生制动和转子腐蚀

paras.en: Light surface rust is not necessarily a problem because normal brake applications can remove it. However, corrosion can progress when friction brakes are not used regularly.
paras.zh: 轻微的表面锈蚀不一定是个问题，因为正常的制动操作可以将其去除。但是，如果不定期使用摩擦制动器，腐蚀可能会加剧。

paras.en: Over time, heavier rust, pitting and scaling can develop on the rotors. Once the rotor surfaces deteriorate significantly, normal brake applications may not restore their condition.
paras.zh: 随着时间的推移，制动盘上可能会出现更严重的锈蚀、麻点和结垢。一旦制动盘表面严重恶化，正常制动操作可能无法恢复其状态。

paras.en: Reduced friction brake usage can also extend brake pad life. However, brake components can develop problems unrelated to friction material wear.
paras.zh: 减少摩擦制动器的使用也可以延长刹车片的寿命。但是，制动器部件可能会出现与摩擦材料磨损无关的问题。

paras.en: Corrosion may form around brake pad hardware, caliper brackets, slide pins and other components. Pads can become restricted in their brackets, while caliper components may develop problems from limited movement.
paras.zh: 刹车片硬件、刹车钳支架、导销和其他部件周围可能会出现腐蚀。刹车片可能会在其支架中受限，而刹车钳部件则可能因运动受限而出现问题。

paras.en: As a result, brake components may require replacement because of corrosion or restricted movement rather than normal wear.
paras.zh: 因此，制动器部件可能需要更换，原因可能是腐蚀或运动受限，而不是正常磨损。

paras.en: How Regenerative and Friction Braking Work Together
paras.zh: 再生制动和摩擦制动如何协同工作

paras.en: Electric vehicles still require conventional hydraulic friction brakes to maintain stopping performance.
paras.zh: 电动汽车仍然需要传统的液压摩擦式制动器来保持制动性能。

paras.en: Regenerative braking may become reduced or unavailable under certain operating conditions. These include a fully charged battery, very cold battery temperatures, vehicle stability control intervention or certain system faults.
paras.zh: 在某些操作条件下，再生制动可能会减弱或无法使用。这些情况包括蓄电池已充满电、蓄电池温度极低、车辆稳定控制系统介入或某些系统故障。

paras.en: EV braking systems blend regenerative braking with conventional hydraulic friction braking to provide the stopping performance drivers expect.
paras.zh: 电动汽车制动系统将再生制动与传统的液压摩擦制动相结合，以提供驾驶员期望的制动性能。

paras.en: This makes conventional brake system condition an important consideration, even when regenerative braking reduces normal friction brake usage.
paras.zh: 这使得常规制动系统的状况成为一个重要的考虑因素，即使在再生制动减少了正常摩擦制动的使用时也是如此。

paras.en: EV Brake Inspection and Maintenance Considerations
paras.zh: 电动汽车制动器检查和维护注意事项

paras.en: Technicians should account for reduced friction brake usage when inspecting electric vehicle braking systems.
paras.zh: 技术人员在检查电动汽车制动系统时，应考虑到摩擦制动器的使用减少。

paras.en: Measuring brake pad thickness alone may not provide a complete picture of component condition.
paras.zh: 仅测量刹车片厚度可能无法全面了解部件的状况。

paras.en: EV regenerative braking improves efficiency by recovering energy and can substantially extend brake pad life. However, reduced friction brake usage can also increase the potential for corrosion and restricted component movement.
paras.zh: 电动汽车的再生制动通过回收能量来提高效率，并且可以大大延长刹车片的寿命。然而，减少摩擦制动器的使用也可能增加腐蚀和部件运动受限的可能性。

paras.en: Brake condition assessments should account for both friction material wear and the effects of limited brake usage.
paras.zh: 制动器状况评估应考虑摩擦材料的磨损和有限制动器使用情况的影响。

paras.en: This video is sponsored by Auto Value and Bumper to Bumper.
paras.zh: 本视频由Auto Value和Bumper to Bumper赞助。

articles.title: Niterra President and CEO Mike Schwab on ‘Delivering Trusted Solutions’
articles.author: Alex Crissey

paras.en: This episode of DriveTime features Mike Schwab, president and CEO of Niterra North America, Inc.
paras.zh: 本期《DriveTime》节目将邀请Niterra North America, Inc.总裁兼首席执行官Mike Schwab做客。

paras.en: Schwab said Niterra has evolved well beyond its roots as an ignition specialist while maintaining the quality and reliability associated with its NGK brand. Today, Niterra’s automotive portfolio extends beyond spark plugs to include ignition coils, wire sets, NTK oxygen and technical sensors and rotating electrical products such as starters and alternators.
paras.zh: Schwab表示，Niterra在保持NGK品牌所代表的品质和可靠性的同时，已远远超出了其作为点火专家这一根源。如今，Niterra的汽车产品组合已不再局限于火花塞，还包括点火线圈、高压线、NTK氧传感器和技术传感器，以及起动机和交流发电机等旋转电气产品。

paras.en: Schwab emphasized that quality, integrity, teamwork and consistent execution remain fundamental to Niterra’s business strategy, even as the industry evolves. These principles, he says, guide how the company serves customers, from delivering dependable products and maintaining transparency to strengthening partnerships and addressing customer challenges. Schwab emphasized that execution means consistently delivering on commitments involving product availability, customer service and new product introductions. While technology and product offerings will continue to change, he believes trust, reliability and strong customer relationships will remain essential to the company’s long-term success.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Looking ahead, Schwab said the transition from NGK Spark Plug to Niterra represents a broader transformation rather than simply a name change. While continuing to strengthen its automotive business, the company is pursuing growth in new products, technologies and markets that build on its engineering capabilities. Opportunities in advanced mobility, electric vehicles and other emerging technologies are part of that strategy. Schwab said the Niterra name, derived from Latin words meaning “to shine” and “Earth,” reflects the company’s ambition to contribute to a more sustainable future.

articles.title: National Signing Day Welcomes Young Technicians Into the Industry with Fanfare
articles.author: NAPA

paras.en: National Signing Day: held in the spring, it features young soon-to-be professionals signing letters of intent affirming their path of choice and receiving a scholarship in turn.
paras.zh: 全国签约日：在春季举行，届时即将成为专业运动员的年轻人将签署意向书，确认自己的职业道路，并获得奖学金。

paras.en: College football? No, better: the automotive aftermarket.
paras.zh: 大学橄榄球？不，更好的选择是：汽车售后市场。

paras.en: That’s right: NAPA and Skills USA held their own National Signing Day on May 6, marking the day as a nationwide celebration recognizing students choosing careers in the automotive, diesel and motorsports industries.
paras.zh: 没错：NAPA和Skills USA于5月6日举办了自己的全国签约日活动，将这一天定为全国庆祝日，表彰选择从事汽车、柴油和赛车行业的学生。

paras.en: As with football, the automotive technical industry needs plenty of young people coming into the profession, and like a college that recruits a player to play for them, we need to make them feel at home in the industry.
paras.zh: 与足球一样，汽车技术行业需要大量年轻人加入这个行业。就像一所大学招募球员为其效力一样，我们需要让他们在行业中感到宾至如归。

paras.en: On May 6, NAPA and Skills USA welcomed six students from Georgia to Truist Park, home of the Atlanta Braves, to sign letters of intent and officially commit to careers as automotive technicians.
paras.zh: 5月6日，NAPA和Skills USA在亚特兰大勇士队的主场Truist Park迎来了来自佐治亚州的六名学生，他们签署了意向书，并正式承诺从事汽车技师的职业。

paras.en: Each student received a Carlyle toolbox kit packed with the necessary tools to get their careers going. They knew that was going to happen, but what they didn’t know was that Cassie Bell, chief people officer at NAPA, was going to surprise them with $2,500 scholarships to support their post-secondary education in the industry.
paras.zh: 每位学生都收到了一套Carlyle工具箱，里面装满了开启职业生涯所需的工具。他们知道会发生这样的事情，但他们不知道的是，NAPA首席人力资源官Cassie Bell将为他们带来一个惊喜，那就是为他们提供2500美元的奖学金，以支持他们在该行业接受高等教育。

paras.en: “This is one of my favorite nights of the year,” said Bell. “National Signing Day is a moment the whole country pauses to recognize students stepping into their futures, and we wanted to make sure the students choosing the skilled trades felt that same energy and excitement. We talk a lot about investing in our people, and tonight that means making sure these students know how thrilled the industry is to welcome them.”
paras.zh: “这是我一年中最喜欢的夜晚之一，”Bell说道。“全国签约日是举国上下驻足表彰即将迈入未来的学子们的时刻，我们希望确保选择技术工种的学子们也能感受到同样的活力和兴奋。我们经常谈到要对员工进行投资，今晚这意味着要让这些学生知道，行业对他们的到来是多么兴奋。”
